workaholism.t: n. 工作狂热；沉迷工作

e.en: Therapists increasingly treat {workaholism} as a serious addiction.
e.zh: 治疗师越来越把工作成瘾视为一种严重的成瘾问题。

e.en: Silicon Valley culture often glorifies {workaholism}.
e.zh: 硅谷文化常常把过度工作奉为美德。

e.en: Tools are scattered across the cluttered {workbench}.
e.zh: 工具杂乱地散落在工作台上。

e.en: He built a sturdy {workbench} in the garage.
e.zh: 他在车库里搭了一张结实的工作台。

e.en: The lab has six {workbenches} along the back wall.
e.zh: 实验室后墙边摆着六张工作台。

e.en: Mechanics organized their tools on neat {workbenches}.
e.zh: 机修工把工具整齐地摆在工作台上。

e.en: A small {workboat} ferried supplies to the offshore platform.
e.zh: 一艘小型工作船把补给运到海上平台。

e.en: The harbor was full of fishing {workboat} traffic.
e.zh: 港口里满是来往的渔业工作船。

e.en: Students completed exercises in their math {workbook}.
e.zh: 学生们做完了数学练习册上的习题。

e.en: Open the Excel {workbook} and check the second sheet.
e.zh: 打开这个 Excel 工作簿,看一下第二张表。

e.en: My {workday} usually starts with a quick standup meeting.
e.zh: 我的工作日通常以一个简短的站会开始。

e.en: A typical {workday} in Tokyo can stretch past ten hours.
e.zh: 东京典型的工作日可能会超过十个小时。

worked.t: v. work 的过去式；工作、运转

e.en: She {worked} late to finish the quarterly report.
e.zh: 她加班到很晚才完成季度报告。

e.en: The new marketing strategy {worked} better than expected.
e.zh: 新的营销策略效果比预期还要好。

e.en: Each construction {worker} must wear a hard hat onsite.
e.zh: 每位建筑工人在现场都必须戴安全帽。

e.en: She is a hard {worker} who rarely misses a deadline.
e.zh: 她工作很努力,几乎从不错过任何截止日期。

e.en: Factory {workers} went on strike for better wages.
e.zh: 工厂工人为争取更高工资而罢工。

e.en: Remote {workers} now make up a third of the team.
e.zh: 远程办公的员工现在占团队的三分之一。

workfare.t: n. 以工代赈；工作福利制度

e.en: The state introduced a {workfare} program for benefit recipients.
e.zh: 该州为福利领取者推出了一项以工代赈计划。

e.en: Critics argue {workfare} fails to lift families from poverty.
e.zh: 批评者认为以工代赈无法让家庭摆脱贫困。

e.en: Automating the report builder streamlined our entire {workflow}.
e.zh: 自动化报告生成器简化了我们的整个工作流程。

e.en: She designed a new editorial {workflow} for the team.
e.zh: 她为团队设计了一套全新的编辑工作流程。

e.en: Women now make up half of the global {workforce}.
e.zh: 女性如今占全球劳动力的一半。

e.en: The company plans to expand its {workforce} next quarter.
e.zh: 公司计划在下个季度扩充员工队伍。

e.en: Many tech {workforces} have shifted to hybrid schedules.
e.zh: 许多科技公司的员工队伍已经转向混合办公模式。

e.en: Aging {workforces} pose challenges for European economies.
e.zh: 老龄化的劳动力人口给欧洲经济带来了挑战。

e.en: Each {workgroup} presents progress at the Friday standup.
e.zh: 每个工作小组都会在周五的站会上汇报进展。

e.en: She leads a small {workgroup} focused on accessibility.
e.zh: 她领导着一个专注于无障碍设计的小工作组。

workhorse.t: n. 主力；任劳任怨的人或设备

e.en: This old printer is the office {workhorse}.
e.zh: 这台旧打印机是办公室的主力机器。

e.en: She's the {workhorse} of the entire research team.
e.zh: 她是整个研究团队的顶梁柱。

e.en: In Victorian times, the poor often ended up in a {workhouse}.
e.zh: 维多利亚时代,穷人常常最终被送进济贫院。

e.en: The novel describes harsh conditions inside the {workhouse}.
e.zh: 这部小说描写了济贫院内的恶劣环境。

working.t:
adj. 工作的；可用的
n. 运作方式

e.en: She's been {working} from home since the pandemic.
e.zh: 自疫情以来她一直在家办公。

e.en: My laptop isn't {working} properly today.
e.zh: 我的笔记本电脑今天运转不正常。

e.en: The bar is popular with the local {workingman}.
e.zh: 这家酒吧很受当地工人的欢迎。

e.en: He wrote songs about the struggles of the {workingman}.
e.zh: 他创作的歌曲讲述了劳动者的艰辛。

e.en: My grandparents live in {Workington}, on the Cumbrian coast.
e.zh: 我的祖父母住在坎布里亚海岸的沃金顿。

e.en: The team from {Workington} won the rugby match.
e.zh: 来自沃金顿的球队赢得了橄榄球比赛。

e.en: My {workload} has doubled since the new project started.
e.zh: 自从新项目启动以来,我的工作量翻倍了。

e.en: Managers should distribute the {workload} more fairly.
e.zh: 管理者应当更公平地分配工作量。

e.en: A {workman} came to fix the leaking pipe.
e.zh: 一名工人来修理漏水的管道。

e.en: A bad {workman} always blames his tools.
e.zh: 拙匠总爱怪工具不好。

workmanlike.t: adj. 熟练的；技艺娴熟的

e.en: The team delivered a {workmanlike} performance against the champions.
e.zh: 该队对阵冠军时打出了扎实的表现。

e.en: The repair was {workmanlike} but not particularly elegant.
e.zh: 这次维修做得熟练但谈不上精致。

e.en: The {workmanship} on this leather bag is exceptional.
e.zh: 这个皮包的做工非常出色。

e.en: Poor {workmanship} caused the bridge to collapse.
e.zh: 工艺低劣导致桥梁坍塌。

e.en: I went for drinks with a few {workmates} after the meeting.
e.zh: 开完会后我和几个同事去喝了酒。

e.en: My {workmate} helped me finish the report on time.
e.zh: 我的同事帮我按时完成了报告。

e.en: Several {workmen} were repairing the road outside.
e.zh: 几名工人正在外面修路。

e.en: The {workmen} arrived early to start the renovation.
e.zh: 工人们一大早就到了,开始装修。

e.en: I do a quick {workout} every morning before breakfast.
e.zh: 我每天早餐前都会快速锻炼一下。

e.en: That hike was a real {workout} for my legs.
e.zh: 那次徒步真把我的腿练惨了。

e.en: Her {workouts} usually last about forty-five minutes.
e.zh: 她的健身训练通常持续四十五分钟左右。

e.en: The app suggests {workouts} based on your fitness level.
e.zh: 这款应用会根据你的体能水平推荐训练。

e.en: The factory employs over two hundred {workpeople}.
e.zh: 这家工厂雇用了两百多名工人。

e.en: Conditions for the {workpeople} have improved greatly.
e.zh: 工人们的工作条件有了很大改善。

e.en: Clamp the {workpiece} firmly before you start drilling.
e.zh: 开始钻孔前要把工件夹紧。

e.en: The lathe rotates the {workpiece} at high speed.
e.zh: 车床高速旋转工件。

e.en: Bullying has no place in a modern {workplace}.
e.zh: 现代职场不应容忍欺凌行为。

e.en: Many companies are rethinking {workplace} design after the pandemic.
e.zh: 疫情后许多公司在重新思考办公空间的设计。

workplaces.t: n. 职场、工作场所（复数）

e.en: Hybrid {workplaces} have become the new normal.
e.zh: 混合办公模式已成为新常态。

e.en: Safety standards vary widely across different {workplaces}.
e.zh: 不同工作场所的安全标准差异很大。

e.en: She designs all her dresses in a small {workroom} upstairs.
e.zh: 她在楼上一间小工作室里设计所有的裙子。

e.en: The artist's {workroom} was cluttered with half-finished canvases.
e.zh: 艺术家的工作室里堆满了未完成的画布。

works.t:
n. 作品；工厂
v. 工作（第三人称单数）

e.en: This remote control no longer {works}.
e.zh: 这个遥控器已经不能用了。

e.en: The museum displays the early {works} of Picasso.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了毕加索早期的作品。

e.en: The teacher handed out a math {worksheet} to each student.
e.zh: 老师给每个学生发了一张数学练习题。

e.en: Open a new {worksheet} in Excel to track expenses.
e.zh: 在 Excel 中新建一个工作表来记录开支。

e.en: I attended a writing {workshop} last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末我参加了一个写作工作坊。

e.en: He repairs old motorcycles in his garage {workshop}.
e.zh: 他在车库改成的工坊里修理老式摩托车。

e.en: The conference offers free {workshops} on machine learning.
e.zh: 该会议提供免费的机器学习研讨班。

e.en: Local {workshops} produce handmade leather goods.
e.zh: 当地的作坊生产手工皮具。

e.en: All visitors must wear hard hats on the {worksite}.
e.zh: 所有访客在工地上都必须戴安全帽。

e.en: The foreman inspected the {worksite} before sunrise.
e.zh: 工头在日出前检查了工地。

e.en: A clean {workspace} helps me focus better.
e.zh: 整洁的工作空间能让我更专注。

e.en: You can switch between {workspaces} with this shortcut.
e.zh: 用这个快捷键可以在工作区之间切换。

e.en: Each engineer has a dual-monitor {workstation}.
e.zh: 每位工程师都有一个配双屏的工作站。

e.en: Please log out of your {workstation} before leaving.
e.zh: 离开前请退出你的工作站登录。

e.en: She spread the fabric across the long {worktable}.
e.zh: 她把布料铺在长长的工作台上。

e.en: The carpenter's {worktable} was covered in sawdust.
e.zh: 木匠的工作台上落满了锯末。

e.en: The classroom has six wooden {worktables} for group projects.
e.zh: 教室里有六张木制工作台供小组活动使用。

e.en: Sturdy {worktables} are essential in any pottery studio.
e.zh: 任何陶艺工作室都少不了结实的工作台。

e.en: Wipe the kitchen {worktop} after preparing raw meat.
e.zh: 处理生肉后要把厨房台面擦干净。

e.en: We chose a granite {worktop} for the new kitchen.
e.zh: 我们为新厨房选了花岗岩台面。

e.en: Iceland is experimenting with a four-day {workweek}.
e.zh: 冰岛正在试行每周四天工作制。

e.en: My {workweek} usually ends on Friday afternoon.
e.zh: 我的工作周通常在星期五下午结束。

e.en: She dreams of traveling around the {world}.
e.zh: 她梦想着环游世界。

e.en: Social media has changed the {world} of journalism.
e.zh: 社交媒体改变了新闻界的格局。

world-wide.t:
adj. 全球的
adv. 全世界地

e.en: The brand has a {world-wide} fan base of millions.
e.zh: 该品牌在全球拥有数百万粉丝。

e.en: The pandemic caused {world-wide} supply chain disruptions.
e.zh: 疫情造成了全球性的供应链中断。

e.en: Travel gave her a quiet {worldliness} beyond her years.
e.zh: 旅行让她在年纪轻轻时就拥有一份沉稳的阅历。

e.en: His {worldliness} made him an effective negotiator abroad.
e.zh: 他见多识广，使他在海外谈判中游刃有余。

e.en: She's young but surprisingly {worldly} for her age.
e.zh: 她虽然年轻，但比同龄人见多识广。

e.en: The monk renounced all {worldly} possessions years ago.
e.zh: 那位僧人多年前就放弃了一切世俗财物。

e.en: Online gaming connects {worlds} that never used to meet.
e.zh: 网络游戏把过去毫无交集的世界连接了起来。

e.en: Their lifestyles are {worlds} apart despite being neighbors.
e.zh: 虽然是邻居，他们的生活方式却天差地别。

e.en: Studying abroad completely reshaped his {worldview}.
e.zh: 留学经历彻底重塑了他的世界观。

e.en: Her {worldview} was shaped by years of volunteer work.
e.zh: 她的世界观是多年志愿者工作塑造而成的。

would.t: v. 将会；愿意（will 的过去式）

e.en: I {would} love to visit Japan someday.
e.zh: 我很想哪天去日本看看。

e.en: She said she {would} call once she landed.
e.zh: 她说一落地就会打电话。

wound.t:
n. 伤口；创伤
v. 使受伤

e.en: The nurse cleaned the {wound} on his knee.
e.zh: 护士帮他清理了膝盖上的伤口。

e.en: Cruel words can {wound} more than a slap.
e.zh: 刻薄的话比一巴掌更伤人。

e.en: Several soldiers were {wounded} in the explosion.
e.zh: 爆炸中有几名士兵受伤。

e.en: His {wounded} pride kept him quiet for days.
e.zh: 自尊受伤让他沉默了好几天。

wounding.t: v. 使受伤（wound 的现在分词）

e.en: The accident left her with a {wounding} scar on her arm.
e.zh: 那次事故在她手臂上留下一道触目的伤疤。

e.en: His {wounding} remarks ruined the dinner mood.
e.zh: 他那些伤人的话破坏了晚餐的气氛。

e.en: Time slowly heals most emotional {wounds}.
e.zh: 时间会慢慢治愈大多数情感创伤。

e.en: The doctor stitched up his {wounds} carefully.
e.zh: 医生小心地缝合了他的伤口。

wove.t: v. 编织（weave 的过去式）

e.en: She {wove} a beautiful scarf from recycled yarn.
e.zh: 她用回收纱线织了一条漂亮的围巾。

e.en: The novelist {wove} three storylines into one ending.
e.zh: 小说家把三条故事线编织成同一个结局。

woven.t:
adj. 编织的
v. weave 的过去分词

e.en: This basket is hand-{woven} from bamboo strips.
e.zh: 这个篮子是用竹条手工编织的。

e.en: Music is deeply {woven} into the city's culture.
e.zh: 音乐深深融入了这座城市的文化。

wow.t:
int. 哇（惊叹）
v. 使惊叹

wrack.t:
n. 毁坏；残骸
v. 折磨

e.en: Don't {wrack} your brain over a silly puzzle.
e.zh: 别为一道无聊的谜题绞尽脑汁。

e.en: Storms left piles of {wrack} along the shoreline.
e.zh: 风暴在海岸线上留下成堆的海藻碎片。

e.en: She was {wracked} with guilt after the argument.
e.zh: 那场争吵后她内疚得不能自已。

e.en: His body was {wracked} by a violent cough.
e.zh: 剧烈的咳嗽让他全身不停颤抖。

e.en: I've been {wracking} my brain trying to remember her name.
e.zh: 我一直在绞尽脑汁想她的名字。

e.en: It was a nerve-{wracking} wait for the test results.
e.zh: 等检查结果的过程让人心力交瘁。

wracks.t: v. 折磨（第三人称单数）

e.en: Anxiety {wracks} him before every public speech.
e.zh: 每次公开演讲前焦虑都折磨着他。

e.en: Guilt still {wracks} her years after the lie.
e.zh: 撒谎多年后,愧疚仍在折磨着她。

e.en: A pale {wraith} seemed to drift through the hallway.
e.zh: 一个苍白的幽灵似乎在走廊中飘过。

e.en: After the illness, he looked like a {wraith}.
e.zh: 那场病后,他瘦得像个幽灵。

e.en: Fog gave the trees a {wraithlike} appearance at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明的雾让树木看起来像幽灵一般。

e.en: Her {wraithlike} figure glided across the ballroom.
e.zh: 她幽灵般的身影飘过舞厅。

wrangle.t:
v. 争吵；争论
n. 争执

e.en: The lawyers {wrangle} over every clause in the contract.
e.zh: 律师们为合同里的每一条款争论不休。

e.en: It took hours to {wrangle} the toddlers into bed.
e.zh: 花了好几个小时才把那些小不点哄上床。

e.en: They {wrangled} for weeks before reaching a deal.
e.zh: 他们争执了好几周才达成协议。

e.en: She {wrangled} a free upgrade to business class.
e.zh: 她软磨硬泡换来了一次免费升级商务舱。

e.en: The {wrangler} rounded up the horses before sunset.
e.zh: 牧马人在日落前把马群赶拢起来。

e.en: She works as a data {wrangler} for a streaming startup.
e.zh: 她在一家流媒体创业公司做数据整理工作。

wrangles.t: v. 争吵（第三人称单数）

e.en: Congress still {wrangles} over the new budget bill.
e.zh: 国会仍在为新的预算法案争吵不休。

e.en: He skillfully {wrangles} messy spreadsheets every Monday.
e.zh: 他每周一都熟练地整理那些杂乱的电子表格。

e.en: After months of {wrangling}, the merger finally closed.
e.zh: 经过数月的争执,这桩并购终于完成。

e.en: Data {wrangling} takes up most of an analyst's day.
e.zh: 数据整理占据了分析师一天中的大部分时间。

wrap.t:
v. 包裹；换行
n. 包装

e.en: Could you {wrap} this gift in pretty paper?
e.zh: 你能用漂亮的纸把这份礼物包起来吗?

e.en: I had a chicken {wrap} for lunch today.
e.zh: 我今天午饭吃了一个鸡肉卷饼。

wraparound.t: adj. 环绕式的；一体式的

e.en: She wore stylish {wraparound} sunglasses on the beach.
e.zh: 她在海滩上戴着时髦的包裹式太阳镜。

e.en: The app has a clean {wraparound} interface for tablets.
e.zh: 这款应用为平板设计了简洁的环绕式界面。

wrapped.t:
adj. 包裹好的
v. wrap 的过去式

e.en: He {wrapped} the gift in shiny blue paper.
e.zh: 他用闪亮的蓝色纸把礼物包了起来。

e.en: The film {wrapped} production ahead of schedule.
e.zh: 这部电影提前完成了拍摄。

e.en: She tossed the candy {wrapper} into the bin.
e.zh: 她把糖果包装纸扔进了垃圾桶。

e.en: This function is just a {wrapper} around the API call.
e.zh: 这个函数只是对 API 调用的一层封装。

wrapping.t:
n. 包装材料
v. 包裹中

e.en: Use recycled paper for {wrapping} the holiday gifts.
e.zh: 用再生纸来包装节日礼物吧。

e.en: The {wrapping} on the parcel was torn during shipping.
e.zh: 包裹的包装在运输途中被撕破了。

e.en: Colorful {wrappings} littered the floor after the party.
e.zh: 派对结束后,五颜六色的包装纸散落一地。

e.en: The mummy's {wrappings} had survived for centuries.
e.zh: 木乃伊的裹尸布保存了几个世纪。

wraps.t: v. 包裹（第三人称单数）

e.en: She {wraps} every order with a handwritten note.
e.zh: 她为每份订单都附上一张手写卡片包装好。

e.en: We ordered chicken {wraps} for lunch today.
e.zh: 我们今天午餐点了鸡肉卷。

e.en: A bright {wrasse} darted between the coral branches.
e.zh: 一条鲜艳的隆头鱼在珊瑚枝间穿梭。

e.en: Divers spotted a cleaner {wrasse} grooming a larger fish.
e.zh: 潜水员看到一条清洁鱼在为大鱼清理身体。

e.en: The manager's {wrath} fell on the careless intern.
e.zh: 经理的怒火发泄在了那个粗心的实习生身上。

e.en: Coastal towns feared the {wrath} of the approaching storm.
e.zh: 沿海城镇害怕即将到来的风暴的肆虐。

e.en: He shot her a {wrathful} glance across the table.
e.zh: 他隔着桌子向她投去一个愤怒的眼神。

e.en: The novel describes a {wrathful} king seeking revenge.
e.zh: 小说描写了一位愤怒的国王寻求复仇。

e.en: She slammed the door {wrathfully} and stormed out.
e.zh: 她愤怒地摔上门,气冲冲地走了出去。

e.en: The coach {wrathfully} criticized the team after the loss.
e.zh: 教练在输球后愤怒地批评了全队。

e.en: Heavy rains can {wreak} havoc on the city's drainage.
e.zh: 暴雨可能会对城市排水系统造成严重破坏。

e.en: He vowed to {wreak} revenge on his betrayers.
e.zh: 他发誓要向背叛者报仇雪恨。

e.en: They hung a pine {wreath} on the front door.
e.zh: 他们在前门挂了一个松枝花环。

e.en: A {wreath} of smoke curled above the chimney.
e.zh: 一缕烟雾在烟囱上方盘绕成环。

e.en: Mist began to {wreathe} the mountain peaks at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时分,雾气开始环绕山峰。

e.en: Smiles {wreathe} her face whenever she sees her grandchildren.
e.zh: 每当看到孙子孙女,她的脸上都洋溢着笑容。

wreck.t:
v. 毁坏
n. 残骸；失事

e.en: One bad decision could {wreck} his entire career.
e.zh: 一个错误的决定可能会毁掉他的整个职业生涯。

e.en: Divers explored the {wreck} of the sunken ship.
e.zh: 潜水员探索了那艘沉船的残骸。

e.en: Investigators sifted through the {wreckage} of the plane crash.
e.zh: 调查人员在飞机失事现场的残骸中仔细搜寻。

e.en: She slowly rebuilt her life from the {wreckage}.
e.zh: 她在废墟中慢慢重建了自己的生活。

e.en: The storm {wrecked} dozens of boats in the harbor.
e.zh: 风暴毁坏了港口里的几十艘船。

e.en: I'm absolutely {wrecked} after that long flight.
e.zh: 经过那趟长途飞行后我累垮了。

e.en: A {wrecker} towed the damaged car off the highway.
e.zh: 一辆拖车把损坏的汽车从高速公路上拖走了。

e.en: He earned a reputation as a home {wrecker}.
e.zh: 他落下了一个破坏别人家庭的名声。

e.en: The {wrecking} ball smashed into the old factory wall.
e.zh: 破拆铁球猛地撞向旧工厂的墙壁。

e.en: Stress is {wrecking} my sleep schedule lately.
e.zh: 压力最近正在打乱我的作息。

wrecks.t:
n. 残骸（复数）
v. 毁坏

e.en: Several shipwreck {wrecks} lie hidden beneath the bay.
e.zh: 海湾下面隐藏着好几艘沉船的残骸。

e.en: Lack of sleep {wrecks} my mood the next day.
e.zh: 睡眠不足会让我第二天心情糟糕透顶。

e.en: A tiny {wren} hopped along the garden fence.
e.zh: 一只小鹪鹩沿着花园围栏蹦蹦跳跳。

e.en: The {wren} built its nest inside an old boot.
e.zh: 鹪鹩把巢筑在了一只旧靴子里。

wrench.t:
n. 扳手
v. 猛扭；扭伤

e.en: He used a {wrench} to tighten the loose bolt.
e.zh: 他用扳手拧紧了松动的螺栓。

e.en: Saying goodbye was a real {wrench} for everyone.
e.zh: 对每个人来说,告别都是一件痛苦的事。

e.en: She {wrenched} the door open with both hands.
e.zh: 她用双手猛地拉开了那扇门。

e.en: He {wrenched} his ankle while playing basketball.
e.zh: 他打篮球时扭伤了脚踝。

wrenches.t:
n. 扳手（复数）
v. 猛拧；扭伤

e.en: The mechanic keeps his {wrenches} neatly in a drawer.
e.zh: 那位机修工把扳手整齐地放在抽屉里。

e.en: She {wrenches} weeds out of the soil every weekend.
e.zh: 她每个周末都从土里使劲拔出杂草。

wrenching.t:
adj. 令人痛苦的；揪心的
v. 猛拧

e.en: The documentary tells a {wrenching} story of survival.
e.zh: 这部纪录片讲述了一个揪心的生存故事。

e.en: He kept {wrenching} at the rusted handle in frustration.
e.zh: 他沮丧地一直用力扭动那个生锈的把手。

e.en: Activists tried to {wrest} control from the corrupt board.
e.zh: 活动人士试图从腐败的董事会手中夺取控制权。

e.en: She had to {wrest} the phone from her toddler.
e.zh: 她不得不从蹒跚学步的孩子手里把手机夺过来。

wrestle.t:
v. 摔跤；搏斗
v. 努力应对

e.en: Engineers still {wrestle} with the same scaling problem.
e.zh: 工程师们仍在为同样的扩展问题伤透脑筋。

e.en: The boys love to {wrestle} on the living room rug.
e.zh: 男孩们喜欢在客厅地毯上摔跤打闹。

wrestler.t: n. 摔跤手；角力运动员

e.en: The {wrestler} lifted his opponent clean off the mat.
e.zh: 那位摔跤手把对手干净利落地举离了垫子。

e.en: She trained for years to become a professional {wrestler}.
e.zh: 她苦练多年才成为一名职业摔跤手。

wrestling.t:
n. 摔跤（运动）
v. 搏斗；角力

e.en: He's {wrestling} with whether to accept the new offer.
e.zh: 他正在纠结是否要接受这个新工作邀请。

e.en: College {wrestling} matches drew big crowds last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末的大学摔跤比赛吸引了大批观众。

wretch.t: n. 可怜的人；卑鄙之人

e.en: The poor {wretch} hadn't eaten in two days.
e.zh: 那个可怜的家伙已经两天没吃东西了。

e.en: Don't trust that lying {wretch} with your money.
e.zh: 别把钱托付给那个撒谎的小人。

wretched.t: adj. 悲惨的；糟糕透顶的

e.en: They lived in {wretched} conditions near the river.
e.zh: 他们在河边过着悲惨的生活。

e.en: The {wretched} weather ruined our weekend hike.
e.zh: 糟糕透顶的天气毁了我们周末的徒步计划。

e.en: He sang {wretchedly} off-key throughout the entire song.
e.zh: 整首歌他都唱得跑调跑得离谱。

e.en: The refugees lived {wretchedly} in overcrowded camps.
e.zh: 难民们在拥挤不堪的营地里过着悲惨的生活。

e.en: The novel captures the {wretchedness} of life in poverty.
e.zh: 这部小说刻画了贫困生活的悲惨。

e.en: Nothing could ease the {wretchedness} she felt that night.
e.zh: 那晚她内心的痛苦难以排解。

wrexham.t: n. 雷克瑟姆（英国威尔士城市）

e.en: {Wrexham} is a town in northeastern Wales.
e.zh: 雷克瑟姆是威尔士东北部的一座城镇。

e.en: Hollywood owners helped {Wrexham} return to the football league.
e.zh: 好莱坞老板帮助雷克瑟姆队重返足球联赛。

wriggle.t:
v. 扭动；蠕动
v. 设法摆脱

e.en: The puppy tried to {wriggle} free from her arms.
e.zh: 小狗试图从她怀里挣脱出来。

e.en: Don't try to {wriggle} out of your responsibilities.
e.zh: 别想推卸自己的责任。

wriggling.t:
v. 扭动；蠕动
adj. 蠕动的

e.en: A {wriggling} worm dangled from the fishing hook.
e.zh: 一条扭动的蠕虫挂在鱼钩上。

e.en: The toddler kept {wriggling} during the family photo.
e.zh: 拍全家福时,小宝宝一直扭来扭去。

wright.t: n. 制造者；匠人（常见姓氏）

e.en: A {wright} once built carts and wagons in this village.
e.zh: 从前这个村子里有工匠制造马车和货车。

e.en: Frank Lloyd {Wright} designed many iconic American houses.
e.zh: 弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特设计了许多标志性的美式住宅。

e.en: {Wrigley} Field is the historic home of the Cubs.
e.zh: 瑞格利球场是小熊队的历史主场。

e.en: {Wrigley} gum has been popular for over a century.
e.zh: 箭牌口香糖畅销已经超过一个世纪。

wring.t:
v. 拧；绞（衣物）
v. 逼取；榨取

e.en: Please {wring} out the towel before hanging it up.
e.zh: 挂之前请把毛巾拧干。

e.en: Reporters tried to {wring} a confession from the suspect.
e.zh: 记者们试图从嫌疑人口中逼出口供。

e.en: The interview put him through the {wringer}.
e.zh: 那场面试让他备受煎熬。

e.en: Grandma still uses an old {wringer} to dry laundry.
e.zh: 奶奶还在用一台旧的拧干机来甩干衣物。

wringing.t:
v. 拧；绞
adj. 湿透的

e.en: She stood {wringing} her hands as she waited for news.
e.zh: 她站在那里搓着双手等待消息。

e.en: He came in from the rain with {wringing}-wet clothes.
e.zh: 他从雨中走进来,衣服湿得能拧出水。

wrinkle.t:
n. 皱纹；褶皱
v. 起皱

e.en: There's a {wrinkle} in the contract we need to discuss.
e.zh: 合同里有个小问题我们需要讨论一下。

e.en: She smoothed out a {wrinkle} on her dress before leaving.
e.zh: 出门前她把裙子上的皱褶抚平了。

e.en: His shirt was hopelessly {wrinkled} after the long flight.
e.zh: 经过长途飞行后,他的衬衫皱得不成样子。

e.en: The {wrinkled} old map showed a hidden mountain trail.
e.zh: 那张皱巴巴的旧地图标出了一条隐秘的山间小路。

wrinkling.t:
v. 起皱；皱起
n. 皱起

e.en: She kept {wrinkling} her nose at the strange smell.
e.zh: 她不停地皱着鼻子嫌那股怪味。

e.en: This fabric resists {wrinkling} even after long travel.
e.zh: 这种面料即使长途旅行也不易起皱。

wrinkly.t: adj. 皱巴巴的；多皱纹的

e.en: The {wrinkly} bulldog wagged its stubby tail happily.
e.zh: 那只皮肤皱巴巴的斗牛犬开心地摇着短尾巴。

e.en: My linen pants always look {wrinkly} after washing.
e.zh: 我的亚麻裤子洗完后总是皱皱巴巴的。

e.en: He fractured his {wrist} after falling off his bike.
e.zh: 他从自行车上摔下来,手腕骨折了。

e.en: The watch fits snugly around her slender {wrist}.
e.zh: 这块手表正好贴合她纤细的手腕。

e.en: Festival guests received a colorful {wristband} at the gate.
e.zh: 音乐节的客人在入口处领到了一条彩色腕带。

e.en: The fitness {wristband} tracks his heart rate all day.
e.zh: 这个健身腕带全天监测他的心率。

e.en: She rubbed her sore {wrists} after typing for hours.
e.zh: 打了几个小时字后,她揉了揉酸痛的手腕。

e.en: Both {wrists} were marked from the tight handcuffs.
e.zh: 紧紧的手铐在她两只手腕上都留下了痕迹。

e.en: He glanced at his {wristwatch} during the meeting.
e.zh: 开会时他瞥了一眼自己的腕表。

e.en: The vintage {wristwatch} belonged to her grandfather.
e.zh: 那块古董腕表是她祖父留下的。

e.en: Collectors paid thousands for rare vintage {wristwatches}.
e.zh: 收藏家花数千美元购买稀有的复古腕表。

e.en: Smart {wristwatches} now monitor sleep and stress levels.
e.zh: 如今的智能腕表可以监测睡眠和压力水平。

e.en: The court issued a {writ} ordering his immediate release.
e.zh: 法院签发了一份令状,命令立即释放他。

e.en: Her ambition was {writ} large across every project.
e.zh: 她的雄心壮志在每个项目中都显而易见。

write.t:
v. 写；书写
v. 写入（数据）

e.en: Please {write} your name on the registration form.
e.zh: 请在登记表上写下你的名字。

e.en: She wants to {write} a novel about her hometown.
e.zh: 她想写一本关于家乡的小说。

e.en: He's a freelance {writer} for several tech magazines.
e.zh: 他是几家科技杂志的自由撰稿人。

e.en: The {writer} signed copies of her new book.
e.zh: 那位作家在她的新书上签名。

writerly.t: adj. 作家式的；文人气的

e.en: His blog has a polished, {writerly} tone.
e.zh: 他的博客带有一种精致的文人腔调。

e.en: She admired the {writerly} ambition in his essays.
e.zh: 她欣赏他文章中那种作家般的志向。

e.en: Many {writers} struggle with self-doubt early in their careers.
e.zh: 许多作家在职业初期都会怀疑自己。

e.en: The festival invited {writers} from over twenty countries.
e.zh: 该节邀请了来自二十多个国家的作家。

writes.t:
v. 写（第三人称单数）
n. 写入操作

e.en: She {writes} a column every Sunday morning.
e.zh: 她每周日早上写一篇专栏。

e.en: He {writes} clean, readable code that's easy to maintain.
e.zh: 他写出的代码简洁易读,便于维护。

e.en: The injured snake began to {writhe} on the ground.
e.zh: 那条受伤的蛇开始在地上扭动。

e.en: His comments made her {writhe} with embarrassment.
e.zh: 他的话让她尴尬得浑身不自在。

writhing.t:
v. 痛苦扭动
adj. 翻滚挣扎的

e.en: The patient was {writhing} in pain on the bed.
e.zh: 病人在床上痛得直打滚。

e.en: A mass of {writhing} worms filled the bait box.
e.zh: 鱼饵盒里满是蠕动的虫子。

writing.t:
n. 写作；文字
v. 书写

e.en: She's {writing} her thesis at the library tonight.
e.zh: 她今晚在图书馆写论文。

e.en: His {writing} has improved a lot this semester.
e.zh: 他这学期写作进步了很多。

e.en: The professor studies the {writings} of ancient Chinese philosophers.
e.zh: 那位教授研究中国古代哲学家的著作。

e.en: Her early {writings} reveal a sharp political mind.
e.zh: 她早期的作品显示出敏锐的政治头脑。

written.t:
adj. 书面的；写下的
v. write 的过去分词

e.en: The report must be {written} in formal English.
e.zh: 这份报告必须用正式英语撰写。

e.en: He has {written} three bestsellers in five years.
e.zh: 他五年内写了三本畅销书。

wrong.t:
adj. 错误的；不对的
n. 错事；不公

e.en: You dialed the {wrong} number again.
e.zh: 你又拨错号码了。

e.en: It's {wrong} to lie to your parents like that.
e.zh: 那样对父母撒谎是不对的。

e.en: The court will punish every {wrongdoer} fairly.
e.zh: 法院会公正地惩处每一个违法者。

e.en: She refused to shield the {wrongdoer} from consequences.
e.zh: 她拒绝替那个犯错的人开脱后果。

e.en: The CEO denied any {wrongdoing} at the press conference.
e.zh: 首席执行官在记者会上否认有任何不当行为。

e.en: Investigators found no evidence of {wrongdoing} by staff.
e.zh: 调查人员没有发现员工有任何违规行为的证据。

wronged.t:
adj. 受到冤屈的
v. 冤枉

e.en: She felt deeply {wronged} by her former employer.
e.zh: 她觉得自己被前雇主严重亏待了。

e.en: The film tells the story of a {wronged} widow.
e.zh: 这部电影讲述了一位蒙冤寡妇的故事。

e.en: He sued the company for {wrongful} dismissal.
e.zh: 他以不当解雇为由起诉了公司。

e.en: The family filed a {wrongful} death lawsuit.
e.zh: 那家人提起了非正常死亡诉讼。

e.en: He was {wrongfully} convicted and spent ten years in prison.
e.zh: 他被错误定罪,坐了十年牢。

e.en: The employee was {wrongfully} terminated without notice.
e.zh: 那名员工在没有通知的情况下被无理解雇。

e.en: The jury debated the {wrongfulness} of his actions.
e.zh: 陪审团讨论了他行为的不当之处。

e.en: She gradually understood the {wrongfulness} of her decision.
e.zh: 她渐渐明白了自己决定的错误所在。

e.en: He was {wrongly} accused of cheating on the exam.
e.zh: 他被错误地指控考试作弊。

e.en: Many people {wrongly} assume the app is free.
e.zh: 许多人错误地以为这款应用是免费的。

e.en: There was a strange {wrongness} about the empty room.
e.zh: 那个空房间透着一种奇怪的不对劲。

e.en: He couldn't articulate the {wrongness} he sensed.
e.zh: 他说不清自己感觉到的那种不对劲。

wrongs.t:
n. 冤屈；不公（复数）
v. 冤枉

e.en: History will record the {wrongs} done to these communities.
e.zh: 历史会记下这些群体所遭受的不公。

e.en: Two {wrongs} don't make a right.
e.zh: 两个错加在一起也变不成对。

e.en: She {wrote} a heartfelt letter to her grandmother.
e.zh: 她给奶奶写了一封情真意切的信。

e.en: He {wrote} the entire app in one weekend.
e.zh: 他一个周末就写完了整个应用。

wrought.t:
adj. 锻造的；精心制作的
v. work 的旧式过去式

e.en: The garden gate is made of {wrought} iron.
e.zh: 那扇花园门是用锻铁制成的。

e.en: The new policy has {wrought} major changes in education.
e.zh: 这项新政策给教育带来了重大变革。

e.en: Doctors use {wrvs} to measure the work involved in procedures.
e.zh: 医生用工作相对值来衡量医疗操作的工作量。

e.en: Higher {wrvs} usually mean more reimbursement for the physician.
e.zh: 工作相对值越高,医生获得的报酬通常越多。

e.en: She smiled {wryly} at his terrible pun.
e.zh: 她对他那个糟糕的双关语苦笑了一下。

e.en: He {wryly} admitted the project was behind schedule.
e.zh: 他自嘲地承认项目已经落后于进度。

e.en: The startup was founded by a coding {wunderkind}.
e.zh: 这家初创公司由一位编程神童创办。

e.en: At sixteen she was hailed as a chess {wunderkind}.
e.zh: 十六岁时她就被誉为国际象棋神童。

e.en: Don't be such a {wuss} — the water's not cold.
e.zh: 别这么胆小,水又不凉。

e.en: He called his brother a {wuss} for skipping the ride.
e.zh: 他笑弟弟是胆小鬼,不敢玩那个项目。

wussy.t:
n. 胆小鬼
adj. 软弱的

e.en: That's a pretty {wussy} excuse for missing practice.
e.zh: 那是个相当怂的翘训练借口。

e.en: Stop being {wussy} and just ask her out.
e.zh: 别那么怂,直接约她出去就好。

e.en: The winds {wuther} across the moors at night.
e.zh: 夜里大风呼啸着掠过荒原。

e.en: She listened to the storm {wuther} against the windows.
e.zh: 她听着暴风在窗外呼啸作响。

e.en: An old {wych} elm stood beside the church.
e.zh: 教堂旁立着一棵古老的光叶榆。

e.en: The carpenter prefers {wych} elm for its tough grain.
e.zh: 那位木匠偏爱光叶榆,因为它的纹理坚韧。

e.en: {Wycliffe} translated the Bible into Middle English.
e.zh: 威克里夫把《圣经》翻译成了中古英语。

e.en: Students study {Wycliffe} in their religious history class.
e.zh: 学生们在宗教史课上学习威克里夫。

e.en: Andrew {Wyeth} is famous for the painting Christina's World.
e.zh: 安德鲁·怀斯以画作《克里斯蒂娜的世界》闻名。

e.en: The museum displays several {Wyeth} watercolors this month.
e.zh: 博物馆本月展出多幅怀斯的水彩画。

e.en: They spent the weekend hiking near {Wyke} village.
e.zh: 他们周末在威克村附近徒步。

e.en: The map shows a small bay called {Wyke}.
e.zh: 地图上标着一个叫威克的小海湾。

e.en: John {Wyndham} wrote the classic novel The Day of the Triffids.
e.zh: 约翰·温德姆写了经典小说《三尖树时代》。

e.en: We stayed at a {Wyndham} hotel near the airport.
e.zh: 我们住在机场附近的一家温德姆酒店。

e.en: {Wyoming} has the smallest population of any U.S. state.
e.zh: 怀俄明州是美国人口最少的州。

e.en: They drove through {Wyoming} on their way to Yellowstone.
e.zh: 他们去黄石公园的路上穿过了怀俄明州。

wysiwyg.t: n. 所见即所得（编辑器模式）

e.en: The editor uses a {WYSIWYG} interface for easy formatting.
e.zh: 该编辑器采用所见即所得的界面,排版很方便。

e.en: Most blog platforms offer a {WYSIWYG} editor by default.
e.zh: 大多数博客平台默认提供所见即所得编辑器。

worthiest.t: n. 杰出人物\na. 有价值的, 可敬的, 值得的

e.en: A {W-particle} can mediate certain weak nuclear interactions.
e.zh: W粒子可以传递某些弱核相互作用。

e.en: The lecture explained how the {W-particle} differs from a photon.
e.zh: 讲座解释了W粒子与光子的不同之处。

e.en: The loose wheel began to {wabble} on the cart.
e.zh: 手推车上松动的轮子开始摇晃。

e.en: His voice seemed to {wabble} when he answered.
e.zh: 他回答时声音似乎有些发颤。

e.en: The table {wabbled} whenever someone leaned on it.
e.zh: 只要有人靠上去，那张桌子就会摇晃。

e.en: The toddler {wabbled} across the room toward her mother.
e.zh: 那个幼儿摇摇晃晃地穿过房间走向妈妈。

wabbler.t: 摇晃物；蹒跚者；态度不定者

e.en: The old chair was a terrible {wabbler} on the stone floor.
e.zh: 那把旧椅子在石地上摇晃得厉害。

e.en: Voters saw him as a political {wabbler} with no firm position.
e.zh: 选民认为他是个立场不坚定的政治摇摆者。

e.en: The lamp {wabbles} whenever the train passes.
e.zh: 每当火车经过，那盏灯就会摇晃。

e.en: Her confidence {wabbles} when the questions become personal.
e.zh: 问题变得私人化时，她的信心就会动摇。

wabbliness.t: 摇晃不稳的状态；摇摆感

e.en: The table's {wabbliness} made dinner awkward.
e.zh: 桌子的摇晃不稳让晚餐变得很别扭。

e.en: She noticed a slight {wabbliness} in his voice.
e.zh: 她注意到他的声音里有一点发颤。

e.en: The old chair felt {wabbly} under him.
e.zh: 那把旧椅子在他身下感觉摇摇晃晃。

e.en: Her handwriting looked {wabbly} after the long trip.
e.zh: 长途旅行后，她的字迹看起来有些歪歪扭扭。

e.en: My uncle is a harmless {wackadoodle} at parties.
e.zh: 我叔叔在聚会上是个无伤大雅的怪人。

e.en: That is a {wackadoodle} idea, but it might work.
e.zh: 那主意很离奇，不过也许能行。

e.en: The cliff contains layers of {wacke} and shale.
e.zh: 这处悬崖含有杂砂岩和页岩层。

e.en: Geologists identified the sample as {wacke}.
e.zh: 地质学家把这个样本鉴定为杂砂岩。

e.en: The room was {wackily} decorated with clocks.
e.zh: 房间用许多钟表装饰得很古怪。

e.en: He smiled {wackily} and changed the subject.
e.zh: 他怪怪地一笑，然后换了话题。

e.en: The stream is {wadable} after a dry week.
e.zh: 干了一周后，这条小溪可以涉水过去。

e.en: They searched for a {wadable} crossing near the bend.
e.zh: 他们在河湾附近寻找可以涉水通过的地方。

wadder.t: 把东西揉成团的人或工具

e.en: The machine acts as a paper {wadder} for packing.
e.zh: 这台机器充当包装用的纸团成型机。

e.en: As a careless {wadder}, he ruined the clean wrapping.
e.zh: 他随手把纸揉成团，毁了干净的包装纸。

e.en: The old {waddie} rode back before sunset.
e.zh: 那位老牛仔在日落前骑马回来了。

e.en: A young {waddie} helped brand the calves.
e.zh: 一个年轻牧场工帮忙给小牛烙印。

e.en: The {waddies} gathered near the corral at dawn.
e.zh: 拂晓时，那些牛仔聚在畜栏旁。

e.en: Several {waddies} drove the herd across the plain.
e.zh: 几名牧场工赶着牛群穿过平原。

e.en: The toddler moved {waddlingly} toward the door.
e.zh: 那个小孩摇摇摆摆地朝门口走去。

e.en: He advanced {waddlingly} in oversized boots.
e.zh: 他穿着过大的靴子蹒跚向前。

e.en: He carried a heavy {waddy} for protection.
e.zh: 他带着一根沉重的棍棒防身。

e.en: The {waddy} checked the fence before breakfast.
e.zh: 那个牧场工早饭前检查了围栏。

e.en: The lake has a gentle {wade-in} for children.
e.zh: 这个湖有适合孩子的平缓涉水入口。

e.en: They built a sandy {wade-in} beside the dock.
e.zh: 他们在码头旁修了一个沙质浅水进入处。

e.en: The river was barely {wadeable} after the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨过后，这条河勉强还能涉水通过。

e.en: We chose a {wadeable} stretch below the bridge.
e.zh: 我们选了桥下那段可以涉水的河道。

e.en: The coat was made from thick {wadmal}.
e.zh: 这件外套是用厚实的粗羊毛呢做的。

e.en: Farmers once wore {wadmal} through harsh winters.
e.zh: 农民过去常穿粗呢布衣服熬过严冬。

e.en: Her cloak of {wadmol} kept out the wind.
e.zh: 她的粗羊毛呢斗篷挡住了寒风。

e.en: The museum displayed a jacket woven from {wadmol}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一件用粗呢布织成的夹克。

e.en: He {wadna} leave until the work was done.
e.zh: 他不愿离开，直到活儿做完才走。

e.en: In that dialect, she said she {wadna} go.
e.zh: 在那种方言里，她说自己不会去。

e.en: The farmer used his tools as a {wadset} for the loan.
e.zh: 农民把工具作为贷款的抵押。

e.en: Old records mention a {wadset} on the small estate.
e.zh: 旧记录提到那处小地产曾作典当。

e.en: The {wadsetter} promised to repay the debt by spring.
e.zh: 抵押人承诺在春天前还清债务。

e.en: A careful {wadsetter} kept copies of every agreement.
e.zh: 谨慎的典当者会保存每份协议的副本。

e.en: Rainwater rushed through the {wady} after the storm.
e.zh: 暴雨过后，雨水奔流过那条干河谷。

e.en: The caravan rested beside a dry {wady}.
e.zh: 商队在一条干涸的旱谷旁休息。

e.en: She spoke of old {wae} in a trembling voice.
e.zh: 她用颤抖的声音讲起旧日的悲哀。

e.en: The ballad tells of war and {wae}.
e.zh: 那首民谣讲述战争与灾祸。

e.en: The old tale calls him a poor {waesucks}.
e.zh: 那个古老故事称他为一个可怜的悲伤人。

e.en: Do not sit there like a {waesucks} all evening.
e.zh: 别整晚坐在那里像个可怜虫一样。

e.en: The chef sliced the potatoes {wafer-thin}.
e.zh: 厨师把土豆切得薄如纸片。

e.en: They won by a {wafer-thin} majority.
e.zh: 他们以极其微弱的多数获胜。

e.en: The dessert had a light, {wafery} shell.
e.zh: 这道甜点有一层轻薄酥脆的外壳。

e.en: Dry leaves made a {wafery} sound underfoot.
e.zh: 干叶在脚下发出薄脆般的声响。

e.en: A cool breeze began to {waff} across the field.
e.zh: 一阵凉风开始轻轻吹过田野。

e.en: Smoke would {waff} from the chimney at dawn.
e.zh: 拂晓时烟会从烟囱里飘出来。

e.en: The villagers called the stranger a {waffie}.
e.zh: 村民们把那个陌生人叫作流浪汉。

e.en: He lived like a {waffie} between odd jobs.
e.zh: 他靠零工度日，过得像个无业游民。

e.en: She packed her {wafflestompers} for the muddy trail.
e.zh: 她把厚底登山靴装好，准备走泥泞的小路。

e.en: His old {wafflestompers} left square marks in the snow.
e.zh: 他的旧厚底靴在雪地里留下方格印。

e.en: The {waftage} of perfume reached the hallway.
e.zh: 香水的气息飘送到了走廊。

e.en: Sailors watched the {waftage} of smoke from shore.
e.zh: 水手们看着岸上飘来的烟。

e.en: Her silent {wafture} told us to follow.
e.zh: 她无声的挥手示意我们跟上。

e.en: The flag's gentle {wafture} marked the breeze.
e.zh: 旗帜轻轻飘动，显示有风吹过。

e.en: The company reviewed its {wage-cost} figures each quarter.
e.zh: 公司每季度都会审查工资成本数据。

e.en: Rising {wage-cost} pressure affected the factory's prices.
e.zh: 不断上升的工资成本压力影响了工厂定价。

e.en: Higher {wage-costs} reduced the firm's profit margin.
e.zh: 更高的工资成本压缩了公司的利润率。

e.en: Managers compared {wage-costs} across several departments.
e.zh: 经理们比较了几个部门的工资成本。

e.en: Workers protested against the proposed {wage-cut}.
e.zh: 工人们抗议拟议中的减薪。

e.en: A temporary {wage-cut} helped the firm avoid layoffs.
e.zh: 临时工资削减帮助公司避免裁员。

e.en: Every {wage-earner} in the family contributed to rent.
e.zh: 家里每个靠工资生活的人都分担房租。

e.en: The tax change mainly affects the ordinary {wage-earner}.
e.zh: 这项税制变化主要影响普通工薪族。

e.en: She became the only {wage-earning} adult in the house.
e.zh: 她成了家里唯一有工资收入的成年人。

e.en: Many {wage-earning} families struggled with rent.
e.zh: 许多靠工资生活的家庭为房租发愁。

e.en: The union rejected a two-year {wage-freeze}.
e.zh: 工会拒绝接受为期两年的工资冻结。

e.en: A public-sector {wage-freeze} followed the budget crisis.
e.zh: 预算危机后，公共部门实行了工资冻结。

e.en: Classical economists debated the idea of a {wage-fund}.
e.zh: 古典经济学家曾争论工资基金这一概念。

e.en: The factory's {wage-fund} was set before hiring began.
e.zh: 工厂在招聘开始前就确定了工资总额。

e.en: He spent three {wageless} months after the mine closed.
e.zh: 矿井关闭后，他有三个月没有工资收入。

e.en: Many {wageless} workers relied on relatives for food.
e.zh: 许多失业无薪的工人靠亲戚接济吃饭。

e.en: The pamphlet criticized the old {wages-fund} theory.
e.zh: 这本小册子批评了旧的工资基金理论。

e.en: Officials treated the {wages-fund} as a fixed yearly sum.
e.zh: 官员们把工资总额视为固定的年度款项。

e.en: The novel follows a {wageworker} in a steel town.
e.zh: 这部小说讲述一个钢铁城镇雇佣工人的生活。

e.en: A modern {wageworker} may change jobs many times.
e.zh: 现代工薪劳动者可能多次换工作。

e.en: The old {wagger} kept the table laughing all night.
e.zh: 那个老爱开玩笑的人让一桌人整晚都笑个不停。

e.en: She answered like a practiced {wagger}, half serious and half teasing.
e.zh: 她像个老练的打趣者那样回答，半认真半逗弄。

e.en: His {waggeries} lightened the mood after dinner.
e.zh: 他的那些玩笑话让饭后的气氛轻松起来。

e.en: The book preserves the court {waggeries} of an earlier age.
e.zh: 这本书保留了早年宫廷中的诙谐举动。

e.en: A little {waggery} made the dull meeting bearable.
e.zh: 一点戏谑玩笑让那场沉闷的会议变得可以忍受。

e.en: His formal speech ended with unexpected {waggery}.
e.zh: 他正式的演讲最后以出人意料的诙谐收尾。

e.en: The mill paid extra for {waggonage} over rough roads.
e.zh: 磨坊为崎岖道路上的货车运输多付了费用。

e.en: Old accounts list {waggonage} beside the cost of grain.
e.zh: 旧账册把运费列在粮食成本旁边。

e.en: They rode to the picnic in a borrowed {waggonette}.
e.zh: 他们坐着借来的小型四轮马车去野餐。

e.en: The hotel kept a {waggonette} for guests arriving by train.
e.zh: 旅馆备有一辆小型四轮马车接送坐火车来的客人。

e.en: A {waggonload} of hay stood outside the stable.
e.zh: 马厩外停着一车干草。

e.en: He brought a {waggonload} of excuses to the meeting.
e.zh: 他开会时带来了一大堆借口。

e.en: She booked a {wagon-lit} for the overnight journey.
e.zh: 她为这趟夜间旅程订了一节卧铺车厢。

e.en: The old timetable marked which trains carried a {wagon-lit}.
e.zh: 旧时刻表标明哪些列车带有卧铺车厢。

e.en: The farmer delivered a {wagon-load} of apples before noon.
e.zh: 农夫在中午前送来了一车苹果。

e.en: She arrived with a {wagon-load} of questions.
e.zh: 她带着一大堆问题来了。

e.en: The contract included {wagonage} from the depot to the mine.
e.zh: 合同包括从仓库到矿场的货车运输费用。

e.en: Rising {wagonage} made the coal more expensive inland.
e.zh: 不断上涨的运费使内陆地区的煤更贵了。

e.en: A red {wagonette} waited at the station gate.
e.zh: 一辆红色小型四轮马车等在车站门口。

e.en: The family toured the estate in an open {wagonette}.
e.zh: 那家人乘一辆敞篷小型四轮马车游览庄园。

e.en: The porter led us to the {wagonlit} after supper.
e.zh: 晚饭后，乘务员把我们带到卧铺车厢。

e.en: In older travel writing, a {wagonlit} often meant comfort and privacy.
e.zh: 在较早的旅行文字中，卧铺车厢常意味着舒适和私密。

e.en: His {wagsome} remarks kept the children amused.
e.zh: 他那些诙谐的话让孩子们一直很开心。

e.en: The letter has a {wagsome} tone beneath its politeness.
e.zh: 这封信在礼貌之下带着打趣的语气。

e.en: The guitarist used a {wah-wah} pedal during the solo.
e.zh: 吉他手在独奏时用了哇音踏板。

e.en: The baby made a soft {wah-wah} from the next room.
e.zh: 隔壁房间里婴儿发出轻轻的哇哇声。

e.en: The traveler described meeting a {wahabee} scholar in Arabia.
e.zh: 那位旅行者描述了在阿拉伯遇见一名瓦哈比派学者。

e.en: In the old text, {wahabee} was used for a strict reformer.
e.zh: 在那篇旧文中，瓦哈比派信徒一词用来指严厉的改革者。

e.en: The guide introduced her as a respected {wahine} of the village.
e.zh: 向导介绍说，她是村里受人尊敬的夏威夷女子。

e.en: A young {wahine} paddled calmly beyond the reef.
e.zh: 一名年轻的冲浪女子平静地划过礁石外侧。

e.en: A {wailful} cry rose from the dark street.
e.zh: 黑暗的街上传来一声哀怨的哭喊。

e.en: The singer gave the song a {wailful} beauty.
e.zh: 歌手赋予这首歌一种悲号般的美感。

e.en: The wind blew {wailfully} around the empty house.
e.zh: 风在空屋四周哀怨地吹着。

e.en: She sang {wailfully}, as if remembering a loss.
e.zh: 她悲号般地唱着，仿佛想起了一场失去。

e.en: Only the lighter timber was {wainable} on that narrow track.
e.zh: 在那条窄道上，只有较轻的木材能用货车运走。

e.en: The clerk marked the goods as {wainable} after inspection.
e.zh: 检查后，职员把这些货物标为可用货车运输。

e.en: The estate records mention {wainage} for stone from the quarry.
e.zh: 庄园记录提到从采石场运石头的车运费用。

e.en: Heavy rain delayed the {wainage} of grain to market.
e.zh: 大雨耽误了把谷物车运到市场。

e.en: He tightened the {wainrope} before the cart moved downhill.
e.zh: 马车下坡前，他把捆车绳拉紧了。

e.en: The old {wainrope} snapped under the weight of the logs.
e.zh: 旧货车绳在木材的重量下断了。

e.en: The geologist identified {wairakite} in the volcanic rock sample.
e.zh: 地质学家在火山岩样本中鉴定出了水钙沸石。

e.en: Tiny crystals of {wairakite} formed inside the old cavity.
e.zh: 一些水钙沸石的小晶体在旧空洞里形成。

e.en: She tightened the {waist-belt} before climbing the hill.
e.zh: 爬山前，她把腰带系紧了。

e.en: The coat has a soft {waist-belt} that changes its shape.
e.zh: 这件外套有一条柔软的束腰带，会改变衣服的轮廓。

e.en: We stood {waist-deep} in the cold river.
e.zh: 我们站在冰冷的河水里，水深到腰。

e.en: By noon, the team was {waist-deep} in paperwork.
e.zh: 到中午时，团队已经深陷一堆文书工作。

e.en: A {waist-high} fence surrounded the garden.
e.zh: 花园四周围着一道齐腰高的栅栏。

e.en: The grass grew {waist-high} after weeks of rain.
e.zh: 连下几周雨后，草长到了齐腰高。

e.en: The dress has a high {waist-line} and narrow sleeves.
e.zh: 这条裙子的腰线较高，袖子也很窄。

e.en: Exercise can help reduce your {waist-line} over time.
e.zh: 长期锻炼有助于逐渐减小腰围。

e.en: He clipped the radio to his {waistbelt}.
e.zh: 他把对讲机夹在腰带上。

e.en: The robe was fastened with a woven {waistbelt}.
e.zh: 那件长袍用一条编织腰带系住。

e.en: The statue wears only a simple {waistcloth}.
e.zh: 这座雕像只围着一块简单的缠腰布。

e.en: A cotton {waistcloth} was common in the hot climate.
e.zh: 在炎热的气候里，棉质遮腰布很常见。

e.en: The farmer called the thorny bush {wait-a-bit}.
e.zh: 农民把这种多刺灌木叫作wait-a-bit。

e.en: She gave him a quick {wait-a-bit} gesture at the door.
e.zh: 她在门口做了个让他等一等的手势。

e.en: The board took a {wait-and-see} approach to the merger.
e.zh: 董事会对这次合并采取了观望态度。

e.en: We can only {wait-and-see} how the market reacts.
e.zh: 我们只能等着看市场会有什么反应。

e.en: The clinic put me on a {wait-list} for surgery.
e.zh: 诊所把我列入了手术候补名单。

e.en: They had to {wait-list} several students for the course.
e.zh: 他们不得不把几名学生列入这门课的候补名单。

e.en: Her name is still on the {waiting-list}.
e.zh: 她的名字仍在候补名单上。

e.en: The hospital has a long {waiting-list} for treatment.
e.zh: 这家医院的治疗等候名单很长。

e.en: I joined the {waitlist} for the sold-out class.
e.zh: 我加入了这门已满课程的候补名单。

e.en: The airline may {waitlist} you for an earlier flight.
e.zh: 航空公司可能会把你列入较早航班的候补名单。

e.en: The {waitperson} brought water before taking our order.
e.zh: 服务员先送来了水，然后才为我们点餐。

e.en: A good {waitperson} notices when guests need help.
e.zh: 好的侍应生会注意到客人什么时候需要帮助。

e.en: The {waitron} recommended the fish of the day.
e.zh: 那位餐厅服务员推荐了当天的鱼类菜品。

e.en: In some regions, {waitron} is used instead of waiter or waitress.
e.zh: 在一些地区，人们用waitron来代替waiter或waitress。

e.en: The medieval {waiwode} governed the province for his prince.
e.zh: 这位中世纪地方法官替亲王治理该省。

e.en: A {waiwode} often held both military and civil authority.
e.zh: 旧时的地方长官常同时掌握军事和民政权力。

e.en: The carved {waka} moved slowly across the bay.
e.zh: 那艘雕刻精美的毛利独木舟缓缓驶过海湾。

e.en: She studied a short {waka} in her Japanese literature class.
e.zh: 她在日本文学课上学习了一首短和歌。

e.en: The ceremony honored a {wakan} power in the natural world.
e.zh: 这场仪式敬奉自然界中的神圣力量。

e.en: He described the place as {wakan}, beyond ordinary understanding.
e.zh: 他把这个地方描述为神圣而神秘，超出寻常理解。

e.en: A purple {wake-robin} bloomed beside the forest path.
e.zh: 一株紫色延龄草在林间小路旁开花了。

e.en: The guide warned us not to pick the {wake-robin}.
e.zh: 向导提醒我们不要采摘这种延龄草。

e.en: The canoe moved almost {wakeless} through the still water.
e.zh: 独木舟几乎不留尾波地穿过平静水面。

e.en: His departure was quiet and {wakeless}, leaving no scandal behind.
e.zh: 他的离开安静而无痕，没有留下任何丑闻。

e.en: The {wakerife} child listened to rain all night.
e.zh: 那个睡不着的孩子整夜听着雨声。

e.en: She lay {wakerife} with worry until dawn.
e.zh: 她因忧虑一直醒着躺到天亮。

e.en: {Wakey-wakey}, breakfast is already on the table.
e.zh: 醒醒，早餐已经摆在桌上了。

e.en: The nurse said {wakey-wakey} in a cheerful voice.
e.zh: 护士用轻快的声音说，该醒醒了。

e.en: The belt left a red {wale} on his arm.
e.zh: 皮带在他手臂上留下了一道红红的鞭痕。

e.en: The fabric has a raised {wale} running through it.
e.zh: 这种布料上有一道凸起的纹路贯穿其中。

e.en: The strap {waled} his skin after the fall.
e.zh: 摔倒后，那根带子在他皮肤上勒出了鞭痕。

e.en: She chose a thick, {waled} corduroy jacket.
e.zh: 她选了一件厚实的凸条灯芯绒夹克。

e.en: The rough rope was {waling} his palms.
e.zh: 粗糙的绳子正在他手掌上勒出一道道痕。

e.en: The loom was {waling} the cloth with narrow ribs.
e.zh: 织机把布面织出了细窄的凸条纹。

e.en: The doctor did a quick {walk-about} through the ward.
e.zh: 医生在病房里快速走了一圈查看情况。

e.en: The mayor held a {walk-about} in the market.
e.zh: 市长在市场里进行了一次非正式巡访。

e.en: The clinic accepts {walk-in} patients before noon.
e.zh: 这家诊所中午前接收无需预约的病人。

e.en: Their bedroom has a large {walk-in} closet.
e.zh: 他们的卧室里有一个很大的步入式衣帽间。

e.en: He had a {walk-on} part in the film.
e.zh: 他在那部电影里演了一个小配角。

e.en: She joined the college team as a {walk-on}.
e.zh: 她以非招募队员身份加入了大学校队。

e.en: The workers staged a {walk-out} over pay cuts.
e.zh: 工人们因减薪举行了退场罢工。

e.en: Several delegates made a dramatic {walk-out}.
e.zh: 几名代表以突然退席表示强烈抗议。

walk-over.t: 轻松获胜；无人竞争的胜利

e.en: The final became a {walk-over} after two players withdrew.
e.zh: 两名选手退赛后，决赛变成了一场轻松胜利。

e.en: Everyone expected a {walk-over}, but the match was close.
e.zh: 大家都以为会轻松取胜，但比赛其实很胶着。

e.en: The manager gave us a {walk-through} of the new system.
e.zh: 经理给我们逐步讲解了新系统。

e.en: The cast did a slow {walk-through} before rehearsal.
e.zh: 演员们在排练前慢慢走位演练了一遍。

e.en: The hotel is {walk-to} distance from the station.
e.zh: 这家酒店离车站很近，可以步行到达。

e.en: They wanted a {walk-to} school for their children.
e.zh: 他们想给孩子找一所能走路去的学校。

walk-up.t: 无电梯公寓；临街服务窗口

e.en: She rents a small {walk-up} on the fifth floor.
e.zh: 她租住在五楼一套没有电梯的小公寓里。

e.en: The cafe has a {walk-up} window for coffee orders.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆有一个临街点单窗口。

e.en: Old brick {walk-ups} line the narrow street.
e.zh: 狭窄街道两旁是一排老式砖砌无电梯公寓。

e.en: The stadium added {walk-ups} for same-day ticket sales.
e.zh: 体育场增设了当天售票的临街窗口。

e.en: The city improved {walkability} by widening sidewalks.
e.zh: 这座城市通过拓宽人行道提高了步行友好程度。

e.en: High {walkability} can raise neighborhood property values.
e.zh: 较高的步行便利性会提升社区房产价值。

e.en: Our school organized a {walkathon} for cancer research.
e.zh: 我们学校为癌症研究组织了一场慈善步行募捐活动。

e.en: She collected sponsors before the weekend {walkathon}.
e.zh: 周末步行募捐活动前，她先募集了赞助人。

walkaway.t: 轻松胜利；可带走的收获

e.en: The election was a {walkaway} for the incumbent mayor.
e.zh: 这次选举对现任市长来说是一场轻松胜利。

e.en: My main {walkaway} from the meeting was caution.
e.zh: 这次会议给我最主要的收获是要谨慎行事。

e.en: The {walkdown} to the river took twenty minutes.
e.zh: 走下坡到河边花了二十分钟。

e.en: Officials planned a gradual {walkdown} of interest rates.
e.zh: 官员们计划逐步压低利率。

e.en: The reporter carried a {walkid-lookie} into the crowd.
e.zh: 记者带着一台便携式电视摄像装置走进人群。

e.en: Early broadcasts sometimes used a bulky {walkid-lookie}.
e.zh: 早期转播有时会使用笨重的便携式电视摄像装置。

e.en: The guard spoke into his {walkid-talkie} at the gate.
e.zh: 门口的保安对着手持对讲机说话。

e.en: They used a {walkid-talkie} during the old field exercise.
e.zh: 他们在那次旧式野外演练中使用了步话机。

e.en: The stage manager clipped a {walkie} to her belt.
e.zh: 舞台经理把一部步话机夹在腰带上。

e.en: Keep your {walkie} on during the whole shift.
e.zh: 整个班次期间都要保持你的对讲机开着。

e.en: The crew tested the {walkie-lookie} before the live report.
e.zh: 摄制组在现场报道前测试了便携式电视摄像装置。

e.en: A {walkie-lookie} once seemed amazingly modern.
e.zh: 便携式电视摄像装置曾经显得非常先进。

e.en: The hikers used a {walkie-talkie} in the mountains.
e.zh: 徒步者们在山里使用手持对讲机联络。

e.en: Her toy {walkie-talkie} crackled with static.
e.zh: 她的玩具步话机发出带杂音的噼啪声。

e.en: The bartender mixed a strong {wallbanger} for the regular customer.
e.zh: 酒保给那位常客调了一杯烈性的Wallbanger鸡尾酒。

e.en: That puzzle was a real {wallbanger} for the whole team.
e.zh: 那道谜题把整个团队都难住了，简直让人想撞墙。

e.en: The teacher pointed to the {wallchart} during the lesson.
e.zh: 老师上课时指着墙上的挂图讲解。

e.en: A colorful {wallchart} showed the monthly sales figures.
e.zh: 一张彩色墙上图表展示了每月销售数字。

e.en: The gallery displayed a {wallful} of small portraits.
e.zh: 画廊展出了一整面墙的小幅肖像画。

e.en: She kept a {wallful} of notes above her desk.
e.zh: 她在书桌上方贴了满满一墙笔记。

e.en: A woven {wallhanging} brightened the plain room.
e.zh: 一件编织壁挂让朴素的房间明亮起来。

e.en: They bought an old {wallhanging} at the market.
e.zh: 他们在市场上买了一件旧挂毯。

e.en: The architect designed a {wallless} office for easier collaboration.
e.zh: 建筑师设计了无墙隔断的办公室，方便协作。

e.en: They slept in a {wallless} shelter under the stars.
e.zh: 他们睡在没有墙的棚屋里，头顶是星空。

e.en: Students prepared a {wallnewspaper} about local history.
e.zh: 学生们制作了一份关于地方历史的墙报。

e.en: The factory posted announcements on a {wallnewspaper}.
e.zh: 工厂把通知登在壁报上。

e.en: Several {wallnewspapers} appeared in the school hallway.
e.zh: 学校走廊里出现了几份墙报。

e.en: The campaign used {wallnewspapers} to share public messages.
e.zh: 这场宣传活动用壁报来发布公共信息。

e.en: The ceramic {wallpiece} matched the blue tiles.
e.zh: 那件陶瓷墙面装饰和蓝色瓷砖很相配。

e.en: Her new {wallpiece} was made from recycled wood.
e.zh: 她的新壁挂作品是用回收木料做成的。

e.en: He replaced the cracked {wallplate} beside the light switch.
e.zh: 他更换了电灯开关旁边裂开的墙面盖板。

e.en: A painted {wallplate} hung above the fireplace.
e.zh: 一只彩绘装饰壁盘挂在壁炉上方。

e.en: The museum used a {wallwasher} to light the paintings evenly.
e.zh: 博物馆用洗墙灯均匀照亮画作。

e.en: A pressure {wallwasher} removed dirt from the brick surface.
e.zh: 高压墙面清洗器把砖面上的污垢冲掉了。

e.en: '{Waly}, I have lost my ring,' she cried.
e.zh: 她哭着说：“哎呀，我把戒指弄丢了。”

e.en: The old ballad repeats {waly} in every sad verse.
e.zh: 那首古老民谣在每段伤感歌词里都反复唱着“哀哉”。

e.en: The rough sea made my stomach {wamble}.
e.zh: 汹涌的海浪让我胃里一阵翻腾。

e.en: He began to {wamble} down the muddy lane.
e.zh: 他开始沿着泥泞小路摇摇晃晃地走。

e.en: My stomach {wambled} after the long bus ride.
e.zh: 坐了很久公交后，我的胃一直翻腾。

e.en: The tired child {wambled} across the room.
e.zh: 疲惫的孩子摇摇晃晃地穿过房间。

e.en: The boat's motion left him {wambling} and pale.
e.zh: 船的晃动让他胃里翻腾，脸色发白。

e.en: She came {wambling} home after the sleepless night.
e.zh: 一夜没睡后，她摇摇晃晃地回到家。

e.en: The old tale says the beast had a swollen {wame}.
e.zh: 那个古老故事说，那头野兽肚子鼓胀。

e.en: He clutched his {wame} and groaned in pain.
e.zh: 他捂着肚子痛苦地呻吟。

e.en: The market sold fresh {wampees} by the basket.
e.zh: 市场上一篮篮地卖新鲜黄皮果。

e.en: A {wampee} tree grew beside the old house.
e.zh: 老房子旁边长着一棵黄皮树。

wampish.t: 像吸血鬼女郎的；妖艳的

e.en: She wore a {wampish} black dress to the party.
e.zh: 她穿着一条妖艳的黑裙去参加派对。

e.en: The film gave the singer a {wampish} image.
e.zh: 那部电影给这位歌手塑造了吸血鬼女郎般的形象。

wampus.t: 怪物；混乱或怪异的东西

e.en: Grandpa told us a story about a {wampus} in the woods.
e.zh: 爷爷给我们讲了树林里有怪物的故事。

e.en: The machine made a {wampus} noise and stopped.
e.zh: 那台机器发出怪异的响声后停了下来。

e.en: The {wanderoo} lives in the forests of Sri Lanka.
e.zh: 紫脸叶猴生活在斯里兰卡的森林里。

e.en: A keeper pointed out the {wanderoo} in the enclosure.
e.zh: 饲养员指出了围栏里的那只紫脸叶猴。

e.en: She spent her {wanderyear} volunteering across Asia.
e.zh: 她把自己的游历年用于在亚洲各地做志愿服务。

e.en: His {wanderyear} helped him choose a new career.
e.zh: 那段间隔年帮助他选择了新的职业方向。

wandle.t: 蹒跚行走；摇摇晃晃地走

e.en: The tired child began to {wandle} down the path.
e.zh: 疲惫的孩子开始沿着小路摇摇晃晃地走。

e.en: He {wandled} home after the long celebration.
e.zh: 漫长的庆祝结束后，他蹒跚着回家。

e.en: The old fence was made of {wandoo} timber.
e.zh: 那道旧栅栏是用澳洲桉树硬木做的。

e.en: A tall {wandoo} stood at the edge of the paddock.
e.zh: 牧场边缘立着一棵高大的澳洲桉树。

e.en: The plant had {wandy} stems that bent in the wind.
e.zh: 这种植物有细长柔韧的茎，在风中弯曲。

e.en: He lifted a {wandy} branch from the stream.
e.zh: 他从溪水里捞起一根像魔杖似的树枝。

e.en: The carpenter rejected the {waney} board.
e.zh: 木匠把那块边缘未锯平的木板挑了出来。

e.en: A {waney} edge gave the table a rustic look.
e.zh: 未锯平的木边让桌子显得质朴自然。

e.en: The villagers spoke of the {wanion} that followed him.
e.zh: 村民们谈起一直缠着他的霉运。

e.en: A {wanion} on the thief, she cried.
e.zh: 她喊道，愿那小偷遭诅咒。

e.en: The chair looked too {wankle} to sit on.
e.zh: 那把椅子看起来太不稳，不能坐。

e.en: His {wankle} loyalty worried the party leaders.
e.zh: 他摇摆不定的忠诚让党内领导人担心。

e.en: I {wanna} go home now.
e.zh: 我现在想回家。

e.en: Do you {wanna} watch a movie tonight?
e.zh: 你今晚想看电影吗？

wannabee.t: 冒牌追随者；想成为某类人的人

e.en: He dressed like a rock-star {wannabee}.
e.zh: 他打扮得像个想当摇滚明星的人。

e.en: The club was full of celebrity {wannabees}.
e.zh: 那家俱乐部里满是想挤进名流圈的人。

e.en: He looked {wanner} after a week in bed.
e.zh: 卧床一周后，他看起来更苍白了。

e.en: The lamp seemed {wanner} than the candlelight.
e.zh: 那盏灯看起来比烛光还要暗淡。

e.en: The nurse noticed the {wanness} of his skin.
e.zh: 护士注意到他皮肤的苍白。

e.en: A strange {wanness} settled over the winter sky.
e.zh: 冬日天空笼罩着一种奇异的暗淡感。

e.en: She was the {wannest} patient in the ward.
e.zh: 她是病房里脸色最苍白的病人。

e.en: The {wannest} dawn barely touched the hills.
e.zh: 最暗淡的晨光几乎没有照到山丘。

wannish.t: 略显苍白的；有些暗淡的

e.en: A {wannish} glow filled the sickroom.
e.zh: 病房里充满了略显暗淡的光。

e.en: He gave a {wannish} smile and looked away.
e.zh: 他露出有些苍白的笑容，然后移开视线。

e.en: The guards carried {walkie-talkies} during the night patrol.
e.zh: 保安夜间巡逻时带着对讲机。

e.en: Our team used {walkie-talkies} because there was no phone signal.
e.zh: 因为没有手机信号，我们团队用了对讲机。

e.en: The crew kept in touch with {walkies} backstage.
e.zh: 工作人员在后台用对讲机保持联系。

e.en: She takes the dog for {walkies} every morning.
e.zh: 她每天早上带狗出去遛一圈。

e.en: He clipped a {walkietalkie} to his belt.
e.zh: 他把一部对讲机夹在腰带上。

e.en: The child pretended the toy was a real {walkietalkie}.
e.zh: 那个孩子假装玩具是真正的对讲机。

e.en: The clinic accepts {walkin} patients on weekday mornings.
e.zh: 这家诊所工作日上午接待未预约病人。

e.en: They installed a {walkin} freezer behind the kitchen.
e.zh: 他们在厨房后面装了一个步入式冷冻库。

e.en: She kept {walking-on} despite the heavy rain.
e.zh: 尽管雨下得很大，她还是继续往前走。

e.en: The actor was nervous before {walking-on} stage.
e.zh: 那个演员上台前很紧张。

e.en: Grandfather leaned on his {walking-stick} during the hike.
e.zh: 祖父徒步时拄着手杖。

e.en: A {walking-stick} insect was hiding among the branches.
e.zh: 一只竹节虫藏在树枝之间。

e.en: The ranger spoke into his {walky-talky}.
e.zh: 护林员对着他的对讲机说话。

e.en: We gave each child a toy {walky-talky}.
e.zh: 我们给每个孩子一个玩具对讲机。

e.en: The dancer stretched beside the {wall-bar}.
e.zh: 舞者在墙上扶杠旁做拉伸。

e.en: Guests gathered at the narrow {wall-bar} after work.
e.zh: 下班后，客人们聚在狭窄的墙边吧台旁。

e.en: The builder cut a sheet of {wall-board} for the room.
e.zh: 建筑工人为房间裁了一块墙板。

e.en: Moisture had damaged the old {wall-board}.
e.zh: 潮气损坏了旧石膏板。

e.en: They chose a washable {wall-covering} for the hallway.
e.zh: 他们为走廊选了可清洗的墙面覆盖材料。

e.en: The hotel used silk {wall-covering} in the suites.
e.zh: 酒店在套房里使用了丝质壁装材料。

e.en: The old horse looked slightly {wall-eyed}.
e.zh: 那匹老马看起来有点斜视。

e.en: After the long flight, he appeared {wall-eyed} with exhaustion.
e.zh: 长途飞行后，他累得眼神发直。

e.en: A woven {wall-hanging} brightened the plain room.
e.zh: 一幅编织壁挂让朴素的房间明亮起来。

e.en: She bought a small {wall-hanging} at the craft market.
e.zh: 她在手工市场买了一件小壁挂装饰。

e.en: The resort offered {wall-less} huts facing the sea.
e.zh: 度假村提供面向大海的无墙小屋。

e.en: They imagined a {wall-less} office with open collaboration.
e.zh: 他们设想一个没有隔断、便于协作的办公室。

e.en: A brass {wall-light} hung beside the mirror.
e.zh: 镜子旁挂着一盏黄铜壁灯。

e.en: Please switch on the {wall-light} near the stairs.
e.zh: 请打开楼梯旁的那盏壁灯。

e.en: A {wall-like} barrier of snow blocked the road.
e.zh: 一道像墙一样的雪障堵住了道路。

e.en: The cliffs formed a {wall-like} edge around the valley.
e.zh: 悬崖在山谷周围形成了壁状边缘。

e.en: The ancient {wall-painting} showed hunters and animals.
e.zh: 那幅古代壁画描绘了猎人和动物。

e.en: She restored a faded {wall-painting} in the church.
e.zh: 她修复了教堂里一幅褪色的壁画。

e.en: One wooden {wall-panel} was darker than the others.
e.zh: 有一块木质墙板比其他的颜色更深。

e.en: The electrician removed a {wall-panel} to check the wiring.
