e.en: The architect disliked the building's busy, {windowy} facade.
e.zh: 建筑师不喜欢那栋楼繁杂、满是窗的外立面。

e.en: The old boat carried a patched {windsail}.
e.zh: 那艘旧船挂着一张补过的风帆。

e.en: Engineers tested a new {windsail} for cargo ships.
e.zh: 工程师为货船测试一种新的借风航行帆。

e.en: The {windscreen-wiper} squeaked in the heavy rain.
e.zh: 大雨中挡风玻璃雨刷吱吱作响。

e.en: He replaced the broken {windscreen-wiper} before the trip.
e.zh: 出发前他换掉了坏了的挡风玻璃雨刷。

e.en: The {windscreen-wipers} cleared snow from the glass.
e.zh: 挡风玻璃雨刷把玻璃上的雪扫开。

e.en: Her {windscreen-wipers} stopped working during the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨中她的挡风玻璃雨刷坏了。

e.en: A dark {windspout} formed over the empty field.
e.zh: 一根黑色龙卷风柱在空旷田野上形成。

e.en: Sailors watched a thin {windspout} twist above the sea.
e.zh: 水手们看着一根细细的旋风水柱在海面上扭动。

e.en: The farmer checked the {windstick} before spraying crops.
e.zh: 农民喷洒作物前查看了风向杆。

e.en: A bright {windstick} showed the breeze near the runway.
e.zh: 一根醒目的测风棒显示了跑道附近的微风。

e.en: The factory installed a {windsucker} above the furnace.
e.zh: 工厂在炉子上方安装了吸风装置。

e.en: Dust vanished into the noisy {windsucker}.
e.zh: 灰尘被吸进了那台嘈杂的吸风口。

e.en: The {windtalkers} sent coded messages during the war.
e.zh: 风语者在战争期间发送加密信息。

e.en: A film about {windtalkers} introduced their wartime role.
e.zh: 一部关于风语者的电影介绍了他们在战时的作用。

e.en: The morning had a {winterish} chill.
e.zh: 那个早晨带着几分冬天般的寒意。

e.en: She chose a {winterish} palette of gray and blue.
e.zh: 她选了灰蓝色调，显得很有冬日气息。

e.en: The cabin needs {winterization} before the first snow.
e.zh: 第一场雪来临前，小屋需要做防寒处理。

e.en: Proper {winterization} protects the pipes from freezing.
e.zh: 恰当的过冬准备能防止水管冻裂。

e.en: Heavy ice caused {winterkill} in the wheat fields.
e.zh: 厚冰导致麦田里的作物越冬死亡。

e.en: The farmer blamed {winterkill} for the patchy lawn.
e.zh: 农民认为草坪斑驳是冻害死造成的。

e.en: The {winterkilled} plants were removed in March.
e.zh: 那些因冻害死亡的植物在三月被清除了。

e.en: Several shrubs had {winterkilled} after the long freeze.
e.zh: 长时间严寒过后，几株灌木已经冻死。

e.en: Sudden thaws can increase {winterkilling} in grasses.
e.zh: 突然解冻可能加重草类的越冬冻死。

e.en: Researchers studied {winterkilling} in young fruit trees.
e.zh: 研究人员考察了幼龄果树的冻害致死情况。

e.en: Ice cover often {winterkills} shallow ponds of fish.
e.zh: 冰层常会让浅水池里的鱼越冬死亡。

e.en: Severe cold {winterkills} many tender garden plants.
e.zh: 严寒会冻死许多娇嫩的园艺植物。

e.en: They imagined a {winterless} island in the south.
e.zh: 他们想象着南方一座没有冬天的岛。

e.en: A nearly {winterless} year worried the orchard owners.
e.zh: 几乎没有冬天的一年让果园主们感到担忧。

winterlong.t: 整个冬天的；持续一冬的

e.en: The village held {winterlong} evening gatherings.
e.zh: 村里整个冬天都举办晚间聚会。

e.en: A {winterlong} drought damaged the mountain pastures.
e.zh: 持续一整个冬天的干旱损害了山地牧场。

e.en: The old poem praised the silence of {wintertide}.
e.zh: 那首古诗赞美寒冬时节的寂静。

e.en: Travel was harder in {wintertide} than in spring.
e.zh: 冬季出行比春天困难得多。

e.en: There was a sharp {wintriness} in the air.
e.zh: 空气中有一股刺骨的冬日寒意。

e.en: The painting captures the {wintriness} of the coast.
e.zh: 这幅画捕捉到了海岸的冬天般冷清感。

e.en: The sauce had a rich, {winy} flavor.
e.zh: 这酱汁带有浓郁的酒香味。

e.en: A {winy} smell drifted from the cellar.
e.zh: 地窖里飘出一股像酒一样的气味。

e.en: Use a {wire-cutter} to trim the cable.
e.zh: 用剪线钳把这根电缆修短。

e.en: The electrician kept a {wire-cutter} in his belt.
e.zh: 电工把一把钢丝钳放在腰带上。

e.en: The army tested a {wire-guided} missile.
e.zh: 军方测试了一枚有线制导导弹。

e.en: A {wire-guided} tool can move through the narrow pipe.
e.zh: 线导工具可以穿过狭窄的管道。

e.en: They adopted a {wire-haired} terrier.
e.zh: 他们收养了一只硬毛梗犬。

e.en: The {wire-haired} coat needs regular brushing.
e.zh: 这种硬毛被毛需要定期梳理。

e.en: The window was covered with {wire-mesh}.
e.zh: 窗户上覆着一层金属丝网。

e.en: They built a {wire-mesh} fence around the garden.
e.zh: 他们在花园周围建了一圈铁丝网围栏。

e.en: One {wire-pull} opened the old theater curtain.
e.zh: 拉一下绳索，老剧院的幕布就打开了。

e.en: The scandal exposed a political {wire-pull}.
e.zh: 这桩丑闻揭露了一次政治上的暗中操纵。

e.en: Reporters searched for the real {wire-puller}.
e.zh: 记者们在寻找真正的幕后操纵者。

e.en: The {wire-puller} threaded cables through the wall.
e.zh: 拉线工把电缆穿过了墙体。

e.en: The deal involved too much {wire-pulling}.
e.zh: 这笔交易牵涉太多幕后操纵。

e.en: Careful {wire-pulling} is needed in old buildings.
e.zh: 老建筑里进行拉线作业需要格外小心。

wire-recording.t: 钢丝录音；钢丝录音资料

e.en: The archive preserved a rare {wire-recording}.
e.zh: 档案馆保存了一份罕见的钢丝录音资料。

e.en: Early {wire-recording} equipment was heavy and delicate.
e.zh: 早期钢丝录音设备既笨重又脆弱。

e.en: The suspect believed his phone was {wire-tapped}.
e.zh: 嫌疑人认为自己的电话被窃听了。

e.en: A {wire-tapped} line revealed the secret payments.
e.zh: 一条被监听的线路暴露了秘密付款。

e.en: The court ruled the {wire-tapping} illegal.
e.zh: 法院裁定这次电话窃听违法。

e.en: Police requested permission for {wire-tapping}.
e.zh: 警方申请进行线路监听的许可。

e.en: The champion led {wire-to-wire} in the final race.
e.zh: 冠军在决赛中从头到尾都保持领先。

e.en: It was a {wire-to-wire} victory for the home team.
e.zh: 主队取得了一场全程领先的胜利。

e.en: The crowd watched her {wire-walking} above the square.
e.zh: 人群看着她在广场上方走钢丝。

e.en: He learned {wire-walking} from a circus performer.
e.zh: 他从一位马戏演员那里学会了走钢丝。

e.en: The artisan made a {wire-wove} screen for the window.
e.zh: 工匠为窗户做了一扇金属丝编织的纱网。

e.en: A {wire-wove} pattern strengthened the fragile frame.
e.zh: 金属丝编织的纹样加固了脆弱的框架。

e.en: The factory melted each {wirebar} before drawing cable.
e.zh: 工厂在拉制电缆前先熔化每根线材坯条。

e.en: A shipment of copper {wirebar} arrived at the mill.
e.zh: 一批铜线锭运到了轧厂。

e.en: She hung a tiny {wirebird} above the desk.
e.zh: 她在书桌上方挂了一只小小的铁丝鸟。

e.en: The sculpture looked like a {wirebird} in flight.
e.zh: 那件雕塑看起来像一只飞翔的线鸟。

e.en: The {wiredancer} crossed the rope without a net.
e.zh: 那名走钢丝演员没有安全网就走过了绳索。

e.en: A skilled {wiredancer} needs balance and nerve.
e.zh: 熟练的走钢丝演员需要平衡感和胆量。

e.en: The workshop can {wiredraw} copper into fine strands.
e.zh: 这间作坊能把铜拉制成细金属丝。

e.en: They {wiredraw} steel for musical instruments.
e.zh: 他们为乐器拉制钢丝。

e.en: The {wiredrawer} checked the thickness after each pass.
e.zh: 拉丝工每拉过一道后都会检查粗细。

e.en: This old {wiredrawer} still makes precise silver wire.
e.zh: 这台旧拉丝机仍能制出精细的银线。

e.en: {Wiredrawing} turns thick rods into thin wire.
e.zh: 金属拉丝工艺把粗杆变成细线。

e.en: The museum displayed tools used for {wiredrawing}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了用于金属拉丝的工具。

e.en: The necklace used {wiredrawn} gold for extra delicacy.
e.zh: 这条项链使用经拉丝制成的金丝，更显精巧。

e.en: {Wiredrawn} steel is common in strong cables.
e.zh: 经拉丝制成的钢材常用于高强度缆索。

e.en: The machine {wiredraws} copper all day.
e.zh: 这台机器整天都在拉制铜丝。

e.en: He {wiredraws} silver for handmade jewelry.
e.zh: 他为手工首饰拉制银丝。

e.en: The smith {wiredrew} the heated metal carefully.
e.zh: 铁匠小心地把加热后的金属拉成丝。

e.en: She {wiredrew} gold for the delicate chain.
e.zh: 她为那条精细的链子拉制了金丝。

e.en: The designer showed a {wireframe} before building the app.
e.zh: 设计师在开发应用前展示了网页草图。

e.en: The model appeared as a simple {wireframe} on screen.
e.zh: 屏幕上的模型显示为简单的线框图。

e.en: Their {wirehair} has a rough coat and lively eyes.
e.zh: 他们家的刚毛犬毛发粗硬，眼睛很有神。

e.en: The terrier's {wirehair} needs regular grooming.
e.zh: 这只梗犬的硬毛需要定期梳理。

e.en: They adopted a {wirehaired} terrier from the shelter.
e.zh: 他们从收容所领养了一只硬毛梗犬。

e.en: The {wirehaired} coat protects the dog in cold weather.
e.zh: 刚毛皮毛能在寒冷天气里保护这只狗。

e.en: The plant had thin, {wirelike} stems.
e.zh: 这种植物有细得像金属丝的茎。

e.en: A {wirelike} scar ran across his palm.
e.zh: 一道像细线般的疤痕横过他的手掌。

e.en: The company still provides {wireline} phone service.
e.zh: 这家公司仍提供有线电话服务。

e.en: Engineers lowered tools into the well on a {wireline}.
e.zh: 工程师用测井钢缆把工具放入井中。

e.en: The {wireman} repaired the damaged switchboard.
e.zh: 电线工修好了受损的配电盘。

e.en: A trained {wireman} installed the new circuit.
e.zh: 一名受过训练的线务员安装了新电路。

e.en: Several {wiremen} worked through the night after the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨过后，几名电线工通宵抢修。

e.en: The {wiremen} checked every connection in the building.
e.zh: 线务员们检查了楼里的每个接头。

e.en: The newspaper printed a {wirephoto} from overseas.
e.zh: 报纸刊登了一张从海外传来的电传照片。

e.en: A blurry {wirephoto} showed the scene minutes later.
e.zh: 几分钟后，一张模糊的传真照片显示了现场。

e.en: Editors selected three {wirephotos} for the front page.
e.zh: 编辑选了三张电传照片放在头版。

e.en: Old {wirephotos} captured news before digital cameras.
e.zh: 旧时的传真照片在数码相机出现前记录新闻。

e.en: Lobbyists tried to {wirepull} the vote quietly.
e.zh: 游说者试图暗中操纵这次投票。

e.en: Workers will {wirepull} the cable through the conduit.
e.zh: 工人会把电缆拉过导管。

e.en: Everyone suspected a hidden {wirepuller} behind the deal.
e.zh: 大家都怀疑这笔交易背后有个幕后操纵者。

e.en: The {wirepuller} fed cable through the wall.
e.zh: 拉线工把电缆穿过墙体。

e.en: The crane lifted the load with {wirerope}.
e.zh: 起重机用钢丝绳吊起了货物。

e.en: Inspect the {wirerope} before climbing the tower.
e.zh: 登塔前要检查钢丝绳。

wirescape.t: 线缆景观；电线构成的景象

e.en: The artist photographed the city's tangled {wirescape}.
e.zh: 艺术家拍下了城市里纠结的线缆景观。

e.en: At dusk, the {wirescape} above the street looked almost abstract.
e.zh: 黄昏时，街道上方的电线景象几乎像抽象画。

e.en: The {wiresmith} repaired the old screen by hand.
e.zh: 那位金属丝工匠亲手修好了旧纱窗。

e.en: A skilled {wiresmith} can shape copper into delicate art.
e.zh: 熟练的线匠能把铜丝做成精细的艺术品。

e.en: The costume glittered with {wirespun} silver thread.
e.zh: 那套服装闪着由银丝纺成的光泽。

e.en: She bought a {wirespun} scarf at the craft market.
e.zh: 她在手工市场买了一条金属丝织成的围巾。

e.en: The electrician routed the cable through a ceiling {wireway}.
e.zh: 电工把电缆穿过天花板里的走线通道。

e.en: Dust inside the {wireway} made maintenance difficult.
e.zh: 电线槽里的灰尘让维护工作变得困难。

e.en: The factory has labeled {wireways} above every machine.
e.zh: 工厂在每台机器上方都标好了走线通道。

e.en: Separate {wireways} keep power and data cables apart.
e.zh: 分开的电线槽能让电源线和数据线保持隔离。

e.en: He cleaned the rust with a spinning {wirewheel}.
e.zh: 他用旋转的钢丝轮清除了铁锈。

e.en: The vintage car still had its original {wirewheel}.
e.zh: 那辆老爷车仍保留着原来的辐条轮。

e.en: The gate's {wirework} formed a pattern of leaves.
e.zh: 大门上的金属丝工艺形成了叶子图案。

e.en: Her jewelry combines beads with fine {wirework}.
e.zh: 她的首饰把珠子和精细的丝工艺结合在一起。

e.en: A {wireworm} had damaged the roots of the young corn.
e.zh: 一条金针虫已经咬坏了嫩玉米的根。

e.en: Farmers check the soil early for {wireworm} activity.
e.zh: 农民会早早检查土壤中是否有金针虫活动。

e.en: The potatoes were scarred by {wireworms} in the field.
e.zh: 地里的土豆被金针虫咬出了伤痕。

e.en: Crop rotation can reduce {wireworms} over several seasons.
e.zh: 轮作能在几个季节内减少金针虫。

e.en: The radio used a {wirewound} resistor for stability.
e.zh: 这台收音机使用绕线电阻来保持稳定。

e.en: A {wirewound} coil sat inside the small transformer.
e.zh: 小变压器里有一个线绕线圈。

e.en: The old runner moved {wirily} up the hill.
e.zh: 那位老跑者瘦而结实地跑上山坡。

e.en: He smiled {wirily}, all angles and nervous energy.
e.zh: 他刚劲而略显紧张地笑了笑，整个人线条分明。

e.en: Her {wiriness} helped her climb for hours without tiring.
e.zh: 她瘦而结实的体格让她能连续攀爬数小时而不累。

e.en: The actor's {wiriness} made him perfect for the role.
e.zh: 那名演员身上的坚韧感让他非常适合这个角色。

e.en: In this dialect, people still say {wirk} for work.
e.zh: 在这种方言里，人们仍用wirk来表示工作。

e.en: The old remedy did not {wirk} as promised.
e.zh: 那个老偏方并没有像承诺的那样起作用。

e.en: {Wirra}, she cried, what trouble has come now?
e.zh: 她喊道，哎呀，现在又出了什么麻烦？

e.en: The old song repeats {wirra} after every sad verse.
e.zh: 那首老歌在每段悲伤歌词后都会重复一声哀叹。

e.en: I do not {wis} what answer he expected.
e.zh: 我不知道他原本期待什么回答。

e.en: She {wis} that silence would serve her better.
e.zh: 她料想保持沉默会对自己更有利。

e.en: Some {wisehead} decided the bridge needed no inspection.
e.zh: 某个自作聪明的人认定那座桥不需要检查。

e.en: The village {wisehead} settled disputes under the old tree.
e.zh: 村里的智者在老树下调解纠纷。

e.en: Stop being a {wisenheimer} and answer the question.
e.zh: 别再自作聪明了，好好回答问题。

e.en: Every class has one {wisenheimer} who corrects the teacher.
e.zh: 每个班总有一个爱卖弄聪明的人去纠正老师。

e.en: A {wisent} moved slowly through the snowy forest.
e.zh: 一头欧洲野牛缓慢穿过积雪的森林。

e.en: Conservationists helped the {wisent} return to protected woods.
e.zh: 保护人员帮助欧洲野牛重返受保护的林地。

e.en: The villagers asked the {wisewoman} for advice.
e.zh: 村民们向那位女智者请教。

e.en: A {wisewoman} prepared herbs for the sick child.
e.zh: 一位民间女医者为生病的孩子配制草药。

e.en: The ending felt like pure {wish-fulfillment}.
e.zh: 这个结局感觉完全是在满足愿望。

e.en: His plan was more {wish-fulfillment} than strategy.
e.zh: 他的计划更像如愿幻想，而不是策略。

e.en: This soup is thin {wish-wash}, not a real meal.
e.zh: 这汤淡得像清水，算不上真正的一餐。

e.en: The speech was political {wish-wash} with no clear promise.
e.zh: 那场演讲全是政治废话，没有明确承诺。

e.en: {Wisha} I could see home once more.
e.zh: 真希望我还能再看一眼家。

e.en: {Wisha}, he said, that the rain would stop.
e.zh: 他说，但愿这场雨能停下来。

e.en: The team finally received the {wished-for} approval.
e.zh: 团队终于得到了盼望已久的批准。

e.en: Her {wished-for} chance arrived sooner than expected.
e.zh: 她渴望已久的机会比预想中更早到来。

e.en: The king sought counsel from the {witen}.
e.zh: 国王向那些贤人征求意见。

e.en: Old chronicles praised the {witen} for their judgment.
e.zh: 古老编年史称赞这些智者的判断力。

witenagemot.t: 盎格鲁撒克逊贤人会议

e.en: The {witenagemot} advised the early English king.
e.zh: 贤人会议为早期英格兰国王出谋划策。

e.en: Historians debate how much power the {witenagemot} held.
e.zh: 历史学家争论贤人会议究竟拥有多大权力。

witenagemote.t: 贤人会议；古英格兰议会

e.en: A {witenagemote} could approve a new ruler.
e.zh: 贤人会议可以认可新的统治者。

e.en: The novel mentions a {witenagemote} in Saxon England.
e.zh: 小说提到撒克逊英格兰的一次贤人会议。

e.en: The old spelling {with-draw} appears in the manuscript.
e.zh: 手稿中出现了 with-draw 这种旧拼写。

e.en: He chose to {with-draw} his claim quietly.
e.zh: 他选择悄悄撤回自己的主张。

e.en: Her grandmother is surprisingly {with-it} about technology.
e.zh: 她祖母对科技出乎意料地很跟得上潮流。

e.en: After coffee, I felt more {with-it} at the meeting.
e.zh: 喝完咖啡后，我在会议上感觉清醒多了。

e.en: They bought a {with-profit} life insurance policy.
e.zh: 他们购买了一份分红型人寿保险。

e.en: The fund offered {with-profit} returns to long-term savers.
e.zh: 该基金向长期储户提供带收益的回报。

e.en: The cabinet displayed a pale sample of {withamite}.
e.zh: 陈列柜里展示了一块浅色的纤维状重晶石样本。

e.en: A mineral collector identified the specimen as {withamite}.
e.zh: 一位矿物收藏者把这块标本鉴定为 withamite。

e.en: The offer remains {withdrawable} until both parties sign.
e.zh: 在双方签字前，这项报价仍可撤回。

e.en: Only part of the balance is immediately {withdrawable}.
e.zh: 余额中只有一部分可以立即提取。

e.en: His sudden {withdrawment} surprised the committee.
e.zh: 他的突然退出让委员会感到意外。

e.en: The poem describes a lonely {withdrawment} from public life.
e.zh: 这首诗描写了从公众生活中孤独退隐。

e.en: The mine once produced large crystals of {witherite}.
e.zh: 这座矿山曾产出大块毒重石晶体。

e.en: Geologists tested the white mineral and found {witherite}.
e.zh: 地质学家检测这种白色矿物后发现是毒重石。

e.en: The dancer turned {withershins} around the fire.
e.zh: 舞者绕着火堆逆时针旋转。

e.en: In folklore, walking {withershins} was considered unlucky.
e.zh: 在民俗中，逆向行走被认为不吉利。

e.en: The {withholdment} of evidence damaged the case.
e.zh: 证据被扣留损害了这起案件。

e.en: She resented his {withholdment} of affection.
e.zh: 她怨恨他不肯表达感情。

e.en: The baskets were woven from fresh {withies}.
e.zh: 这些篮子是用新鲜柳条编成的。

e.en: Farmers tied the fence with twisted {withies}.
e.zh: 农民用拧过的柔韧枝条绑住篱笆。

e.en: The children stayed {withindoors} during the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨期间孩子们待在屋内。

e.en: She carried the wet clothes {withindoors} before dusk.
e.zh: 她在黄昏前把湿衣服拿进屋里。

e.en: A faint light burned {withinside} the chapel.
e.zh: 小礼拜堂里面亮着微弱的灯光。

e.en: He kept his doubts {withinside} his heart.
e.zh: 他把疑虑藏在心里。

e.en: They slept {withoutdoors} on warm summer nights.
e.zh: 夏夜温暖时，他们睡在户外。

e.en: The noise came from {withoutdoors}, beyond the gate.
e.zh: 声音来自屋外，在大门那边。

e.en: He wandered {withouten} food or money.
e.zh: 他没有食物也没有钱，四处流浪。

e.en: The old ballad says she waited {withouten} the wall.
e.zh: 那首古老歌谣说她在墙外等候。

e.en: He tied the bundle with a green {withy}.
e.zh: 他用一根青柳条把包裹扎好。

e.en: A crooked {withy} grew beside the stream.
e.zh: 溪边长着一棵弯曲的柳树。

e.en: In old law, {witing} could mean blaming a man.
e.zh: 在古代法律中，witing 可以表示责备某人。

e.en: The clerk was {witing} of the hidden debt.
e.zh: 那名书记知道这笔隐秘债务。

witling.t: 自作聪明的人；小聪明者

e.en: The young {witling} mocked every serious speech.
e.zh: 那个自作聪明的年轻人嘲笑每一次严肃发言。

e.en: No one trusted the {witling} with delicate negotiations.
e.zh: 没人放心把微妙谈判交给那个小聪明的人。

e.en: She stood in the {witness-box} and answered calmly.
e.zh: 她站在证人席上，冷静地回答问题。

e.en: The lawyer pointed toward the {witness-box}.
e.zh: 律师指向证人席。

e.en: The quick-{witted} child solved the riddle first.
e.zh: 那个机智的孩子最先解开谜题。

e.en: He seemed slow-{witted} after the accident.
e.zh: 事故后他显得反应迟钝。

e.en: She kept the {wishingbone} from the roast chicken.
e.zh: 她把烤鸡里的叉骨留了下来。

e.en: The children pulled the {wishingbone} after dinner.
e.zh: 孩子们晚饭后拉开那块许愿骨。

e.en: This camera is on my {wishlist}.
e.zh: 这台相机在我的心愿单上。

e.en: The charity published a {wishlist} for donations.
e.zh: 这家慈善机构公布了一份捐赠愿望清单。

e.en: His {wishy-washiness} frustrated the whole team.
e.zh: 他的优柔寡断让整个团队很沮丧。

e.en: The speech was criticized for its {wishy-washiness}.
e.zh: 这篇演讲因立场含糊软弱而受到批评。

wishy-washy.t: 优柔寡断的；软弱含糊的

e.en: Don't give me a {wishy-washy} answer.
e.zh: 别给我一个含糊软弱的回答。

e.en: The policy sounded {wishy-washy} and unclear.
e.zh: 这项政策听起来优柔寡断又不清楚。

e.en: The {wisperer} stood close to the doorway.
e.zh: 那个低声说话的人站在门口附近。

e.en: A nervous {wisperer} passed the message along.
e.zh: 一个紧张的耳语者把消息传了下去。

e.en: Smoke rose {wispily} from the chimney.
e.zh: 烟从烟囱里一缕缕地升起。

e.en: Her hair fell {wispily} around her face.
e.zh: 她的头发细细散落在脸旁。

e.en: The artist liked the {wispiness} of the clouds.
e.zh: 这位艺术家喜欢云朵那种轻薄缕状感。

e.en: Her voice had a strange {wispiness}.
e.zh: 她的声音有一种奇异的纤弱感。

e.en: A {wispish} cloud crossed the moon.
e.zh: 一片纤薄如缕的云掠过月亮。

e.en: He had a {wispish} beard on his chin.
e.zh: 他的下巴上留着稀疏纤细的胡子。

e.en: A {wisplike} trail of smoke remained.
e.zh: 空气中还留着一缕似的烟迹。

e.en: Her {wisplike} figure disappeared in the fog.
e.zh: 她纤细的身影消失在雾中。

e.en: He {wist} not what danger waited outside.
e.zh: 他不知道外面有什么危险在等着。

e.en: Little she {wist} of the plan against her.
e.zh: 她几乎不晓得有人在密谋对付她。

e.en: The old wall was covered with {wistaria}.
e.zh: 那面旧墙爬满了紫藤。

e.en: Purple {wistaria} hung over the garden path.
e.zh: 紫色的紫藤垂在花园小路上方。

witan.t: 贤人会议；盎格鲁撒克逊议会

e.en: The king consulted the {witan} before acting.
e.zh: 国王行动前先征询贤人会议的意见。

e.en: Historians debate the power of the {witan}.
e.zh: 历史学家争论盎格鲁撒克逊贤人会议的权力。

e.en: The inquiry became a political {witch-hunt}.
e.zh: 这次调查变成了一场政治迫害。

e.en: The village began a {witch-hunt} after the rumors.
e.zh: 谣言传开后，村子开始搜捕所谓女巫。

witch-hunter.t: 搜捕女巫者；迫害异己者

e.en: The {witch-hunter} accused several innocent women.
e.zh: 那个搜捕女巫的人指控了几名无辜女子。

e.en: He acted like a political {witch-hunter}.
e.zh: 他的做派像个迫害异己的政治打手。

e.en: The committee was accused of {witch-hunting}.
e.zh: 该委员会被指责在迫害异己。

e.en: Medieval {witch-hunting} spread fear across villages.
e.zh: 中世纪的搜捕女巫在村庄间散播恐惧。

witch-hunts.t: 政治迫害；搜捕女巫行动

e.en: The senator denounced the investigations as {witch-hunts}.
e.zh: 那位参议员谴责这些调查是政治迫害。

e.en: Old records describe several local {witch-hunts}.
e.zh: 旧记录描述了几次地方性的搜捕女巫行动。

e.en: The villagers asked the {witchdoctor} for help.
e.zh: 村民们向巫医求助。

e.en: A {witchdoctor} performed the old healing ritual.
e.zh: 一名巫医举行了古老的疗愈仪式。

e.en: They cooked a {witchetty} grub over the fire.
e.zh: 他们在火上烤了一条澳洲木蛾幼虫。

e.en: The guide pointed to a {witchetty} grub in the wood.
e.zh: 向导指着木头里的一条澳洲木蛾幼虫。

e.en: {Witchgrass} spread quickly through the vegetable bed.
e.zh: 茅草很快蔓延到了菜畦里。

e.en: The farmer struggled to remove {witchgrass}.
e.zh: 农民费力清除田里的匍匐冰草。

e.en: She gave a {witchlike} laugh in the dark.
e.zh: 她在黑暗中发出像女巫一样的笑声。

e.en: The old tree had a {witchlike} shape.
e.zh: 那棵老树的形状阴森怪异，像个女巫。

e.en: The tribe respected the old {witchman}.
e.zh: 部落里的人尊敬那位老男巫。

e.en: A {witchman} was called to explain the illness.
e.zh: 人们请来一位巫医解释这种病。

e.en: {Witchweed} can destroy a field of corn.
e.zh: 独脚金可能毁掉一整片玉米地。

e.en: Farmers monitor crops for {witchweed}.
e.zh: 农民会监测作物中是否有这种寄生杂草。

e.en: The tale begins with a lonely {witchwoman}.
e.zh: 这个故事从一位孤独的女巫开始。

e.en: The sick child was taken to a {witchwoman}.
e.zh: 那个生病的孩子被带去见一位女巫医。

e.en: Do not {wite} me for his mistake.
e.zh: 不要因他的错误而责备我。

e.en: The old law set a {wite} for the offense.
e.zh: 古老的法律为这项罪行规定了罚金。

e.en: The {wobbliness} of the table made dinner awkward.
e.zh: 桌子的摇晃不稳让这顿饭吃得很别扭。

e.en: She noticed a slight {wobbliness} in his voice.
e.zh: 她听出他的声音有点发颤。

e.en: The loose wheel began to {wobbulate} on the axle.
e.zh: 松动的轮子开始在轴上摇摆。

e.en: He tried to {wobbulate} the signal for comic effect.
e.zh: 他故意让信号忽强忽弱来制造滑稽效果。

e.en: The technician adjusted the {wobbulator} before the test.
e.zh: 技术员在测试前调好了摇摆调制装置。

e.en: An old radio lab might still have a {wobbulator}.
e.zh: 老式无线电实验室里可能还留着一台扫频调制器。

e.en: He looked {wobegone} after hearing the news.
e.zh: 听到这个消息后，他显得愁眉苦脸。

e.en: The room had a {wobegone} air of neglect.
e.zh: 这个房间透着一种被冷落的凄凉感。

e.en: The shelf {wobs} whenever the train passes.
e.zh: 每当火车经过，架子就会摇晃。

e.en: Her handwriting {wobs} near the end of the letter.
e.zh: 信的末尾处，她的字迹有些发抖。

e.en: The bread was {wodgy} and hard to swallow.
e.zh: 这块面包又湿又黏，很难咽下去。

e.en: He wore a {wodgy} old coat in the rain.
e.zh: 雨中他穿着一件笨重的旧外套。

e.en: She sang a {woesome} song by the fire.
e.zh: 她在炉火旁唱了一首悲伤的歌。

e.en: The abandoned house made a {woesome} sight.
e.zh: 那座废弃的房子看起来十分凄凉。

e.en: They heard a {woful} cry in the night.
e.zh: 他们在夜里听见一声凄惨的叫喊。

e.en: His spelling was {woful} in the exam.
e.zh: 他考试中的拼写糟糕透了。

e.en: She spoke {wofully} of her lost home.
e.zh: 她悲伤地谈起自己失去的家。

e.en: The team was {wofully} unprepared for the match.
e.zh: 这支队伍对比赛准备得糟糕透了。

e.en: The poem's {wofulness} moved the audience.
e.zh: 这首诗的悲伤情绪打动了观众。

e.en: There was a quiet {wofulness} in the old man's smile.
e.zh: 那位老人微笑中带着一种静静的哀伤。

e.en: His scout scarf was held by a leather {woggle}.
e.zh: 他的童军领巾用一个皮制领巾环固定着。

e.en: Don't {woggle} the handle while the machine is running.
e.zh: 机器运转时不要摇动把手。

wogland.t: 种族蔑称中的外国地区

e.en: The novel uses {wogland} to expose colonial prejudice.
e.zh: 这部小说用 wogland 一词揭露殖民偏见。

e.en: He apologized for calling the country {wogland}.
e.zh: 他为把那个国家称作带歧视意味的 wogland 而道歉。

e.en: The study measured {wogonin} in the plant extract.
e.zh: 这项研究测量了植物提取物中的黄芩素类化合物含量。

e.en: Researchers tested whether {wogonin} affected inflammation.
e.zh: 研究人员测试了 wogonin 是否会影响炎症反应。

e.en: The healer warned that {wolf's-bane} is highly poisonous.
e.zh: 医者警告说乌头毒性很强。

e.en: Legends say {wolf's-bane} can repel werewolves.
e.zh: 传说中狼毒草可以驱赶狼人。

e.en: The old herbal lists mention {wolf's-claws} as a plant name.
e.zh: 旧草药名录中把 wolf's-claws 作为一种植物名提到。

e.en: The tracks showed marks like {wolf's-claws} in the mud.
e.zh: 泥地里的足迹留下了像狼爪一样的痕迹。

e.en: The geologist identified {wittichenite} in the dark ore sample.
e.zh: 地质学家在那块深色矿石样本中认出了辉铋铜矿。

e.en: Collectors prize {wittichenite} for its unusual metallic luster.
e.zh: 收藏者看重辉铋铜矿，因为它有不寻常的金属光泽。

e.en: She tried to {witticize} every awkward silence at dinner.
e.zh: 她试图用俏皮话化解晚餐时每一次尴尬的沉默。

e.en: The columnist would {witticize} even the driest policy debate.
e.zh: 那位专栏作家连最枯燥的政策辩论也会写得机智风趣。

e.en: Her {wittiness} made the interview feel effortless.
e.zh: 她的风趣让这场采访显得轻松自然。

e.en: The play relies on {wittiness} rather than loud jokes.
e.zh: 这部戏靠的是机智幽默，而不是夸张的笑料。

e.en: He was a {witting} participant in the fraud.
e.zh: 他是这起欺诈案中知情的参与者。

e.en: No {witting} insult was intended by the remark.
e.zh: 那句话并没有故意冒犯的意思。

e.en: The old comedy mocked him as a foolish {wittol}.
e.zh: 那出老喜剧把他讥讽成一个愚蠢的纵妻不忠者。

e.en: In the poem, the {wittol} knows more than he admits.
e.zh: 在诗中，这个纵容妻子不忠的丈夫知道的比他承认的更多。

e.en: The young lord hoped to {wive} before winter.
e.zh: 那位年轻贵族希望在冬天前娶妻。

e.en: In that village, daughters were expected to {wive} early.
e.zh: 在那个村子里，女儿们通常被期望早早嫁人。

e.en: He had {wived} well, according to the neighbors.
e.zh: 邻居们说，他娶了一位好妻子。

e.en: Once {wived}, she rarely returned to her childhood home.
e.zh: 嫁人之后，她很少再回童年的家。

e.en: A golden {wivern} guarded the shield in the painting.
e.zh: 画中一条金色双足飞龙守护着盾牌。

e.en: The inn sign showed a red {wivern} with spread wings.
e.zh: 客栈招牌上画着一条张开翅膀的红色双足飞龙。

e.en: His family pressed him toward {wiving} and settling down.
e.zh: 他的家人催他娶妻安定下来。

e.en: The ballads treat {wiving} as both duty and fortune.
e.zh: 那些民谣把婚娶既写成责任，也写成命运。

e.en: The fossil of {wiwaxia} shows rows of tiny spines.
e.zh: 威瓦霞虫化石显示出一排排细小的刺。

e.en: Scientists debate where {wiwaxia} fits in early animal evolution.
e.zh: 科学家争论威瓦霞虫在早期动物演化中的位置。

e.en: A {wizzled} apple sat forgotten on the shelf.
e.zh: 一个干瘪起皱的苹果被遗忘在架子上。

e.en: His {wizzled} hands still moved with surprising skill.
e.zh: 他干瘦起皱的双手依然动作熟练得惊人。

e.en: The manuscript spells {wo-man} with a hyphen.
e.zh: 这份手稿把“女人”一词写成带连字符的形式。

e.en: In the old sermon, {wo-man} is treated as a separate word.
e.zh: 在那篇旧布道文中，“女人”被当作一个分开的词来解释。

e.en: The hillside was bright with yellow {woadwaxen}.
e.zh: 山坡上开满黄色染料木，显得十分明亮。

e.en: Old dyers sometimes gathered {woadwaxen} for its color.
e.zh: 旧时染工有时采集染料木来取色。

e.en: The cloth was stained with {woald} from the dye pot.
e.zh: 那块布被染缸里的菘蓝染上了颜色。

e.en: Farmers once grew {woald} for blue pigment.
e.zh: 农民过去曾种植菘蓝来提取蓝色颜料。

e.en: The traveler described a {woback} in his notebook.
e.zh: 旅行者在笔记本里描述了一只袋熊。

e.en: An old dictionary lists {woback} as a name for the wombat.
e.zh: 一本旧词典把woback列为袋熊的一个名称。

e.en: A {wobbegong} lay hidden on the sandy seabed.
e.zh: 一条须鲨藏在沙质海底上。

e.en: Divers watched the {wobbegong} blend into the reef.
e.zh: 潜水员看着那条须鲨融入礁石环境。

e.en: The therapist asked me to stand on a {wobbleboard}.
e.zh: 理疗师让我站到一块摇晃板上。

e.en: The musician bent the {wobbleboard} to make a comic sound.
e.zh: 那位乐手弯动颤音板，发出滑稽的声音。

e.en: This chair is {wobblier} than the old one.
e.zh: 这把椅子比旧的那把更摇晃。

e.en: Her voice grew {wobblier} as the speech continued.
e.zh: 随着演讲继续，她的声音变得更不稳。

e.en: Choose the {wobbliest} table for repair first.
e.zh: 先挑那张最摇晃的桌子来修。

e.en: His first step was the {wobbliest} of all.
e.zh: 他的第一步是所有步子里最不稳的。

wolf-whistle.t: 吹口哨调戏人；挑逗口哨声

e.en: A man gave a {wolf-whistle} as she walked past.
e.zh: 她走过去时，一个男人吹了声调戏的口哨。

e.en: The scene includes a comic {wolf-whistle} from the crowd.
e.zh: 这个场景里有人群中传来一声滑稽的挑逗口哨。

e.en: Some builders {wolf-whistled} at the actress.
e.zh: 几个建筑工人朝那位女演员吹口哨调戏。

e.en: He was criticized after he {wolf-whistled} at a passerby.
e.zh: 他朝路人吹调戏口哨后受到了批评。

wolf-whistles.t: 调戏口哨声；吹口哨调戏

e.en: She ignored the rude {wolf-whistles} from the street.
e.zh: 她没有理会街上传来的粗鲁调戏口哨声。

e.en: He {wolf-whistles} whenever he wants cheap attention.
e.zh: 他想博眼球时就会吹那种轻佻的口哨。

e.en: The company banned {wolf-whistling} on the work site.
e.zh: 公司禁止在工地上吹调戏口哨骚扰他人。

e.en: His {wolf-whistling} was meant as a joke, but it offended her.
e.zh: 他吹调戏口哨本想开玩笑，却冒犯了她。

e.en: The old herbalist warned that {wolfbane} can be poisonous.
e.zh: 那位老草药师警告说乌头可能有毒。

e.en: In the legend, {wolfbane} kept the monster away.
e.zh: 在传说里，避狼草能把怪物赶走。

e.en: She added dried {wolfberries} to the soup.
e.zh: 她把干枸杞子加进汤里。

e.en: The market sells red {wolfberries} by weight.
e.zh: 市场按重量出售红色枸杞子。

e.en: A handful of {wolfberry} sweetened the rice porridge.
e.zh: 一小把枸杞让米粥带了甜味。

e.en: The label says the tea contains {wolfberry} and chrysanthemum.
e.zh: 标签上写着这种茶含有枸杞和菊花。

e.en: The collector identified the dark crystal as {wolfeite}.
e.zh: 收藏者把那块深色晶体鉴定为磷酸铁锰矿。

e.en: Small grains of {wolfeite} appeared in the rock sample.
e.zh: 岩石样本中出现了细小的磷酸铁锰矿颗粒。

e.en: The {wolfess} guarded her cubs near the den.
e.zh: 那只母狼在洞穴旁守护幼崽。

e.en: The novel calls the fierce queen a {wolfess}.
e.zh: 小说把那位凶悍的女王称作母狼般的女人。

e.en: The fisherman pulled a large {wolffish} from the cold water.
e.zh: 渔夫从冰冷的水里钓起一条大狼鱼。

e.en: A {wolffish} uses strong teeth to crush shellfish.
e.zh: 狼鱼会用强壮的牙齿咬碎贝类。

e.en: The fantasy game lets players join the {wolfkin}.
e.zh: 这款奇幻游戏允许玩家加入狼族。

e.en: In the poem, the lonely wolf calls to his {wolfkin}.
e.zh: 诗中那匹孤狼呼唤自己的狼类同伴。

e.en: The dog had a {wolflike} face and pale eyes.
e.zh: 那只狗有一张像狼的脸和浅色眼睛。

e.en: He watched the deal with {wolflike} patience.
e.zh: 他以狼一般的耐心观察这笔交易。

e.en: The ranger found a hungry {wolfling} near the river.
e.zh: 护林员在河边发现了一只饥饿的小狼。

e.en: She drew a {wolfling} curled beneath the moon.
e.zh: 她画了一只蜷在月光下的狼崽。

e.en: Old chemistry books sometimes call tungsten {wolfram}.
e.zh: 旧化学书有时把钨称为wolfram。

e.en: The symbol W comes from the name {wolfram}.
e.zh: 元素符号W来源于wolfram这个名称。

e.en: The lab prepared a {wolframic} acid solution.
e.zh: 实验室配制了一种钨酸溶液。

e.en: They measured the {wolframic} compounds in the ore.
e.zh: 他们测量了矿石中的含钨化合物。

e.en: The antique chart listed tungsten as {wolframinium}.
e.zh: 那张古旧图表把钨列为wolframinium。

e.en: Few modern chemists use the name {wolframinium}.
e.zh: 现代化学家很少使用wolframinium这个名称。

e.en: The mine produced {wolframite} for the steel industry.
e.zh: 这座矿为钢铁工业生产黑钨矿。

e.en: Heavy black {wolframite} was found in the vein.
e.zh: 矿脉中发现了沉重的黑色黑钨矿。

e.en: Some European texts once used {wolframium} for tungsten.
e.zh: 一些欧洲文献曾用wolframium来指钨。

e.en: The museum label explains that {wolframium} is an old name.
e.zh: 博物馆标签说明wolframium是一个旧称。

e.en: The puppy looked oddly {wolfy} in the snow.
e.zh: 那只小狗在雪地里看起来有点像狼。

e.en: The actor gave the villain a {wolfy} grin.
e.zh: 演员给那个反派露出一个狼一般的笑。

e.en: The ceramic factory uses {wollastonite} as a raw material.
e.zh: 这家陶瓷厂把硅灰石作为原料使用。

e.en: White needles of {wollastonite} lined the fracture.
e.zh: 裂缝里排列着白色针状硅灰石。

e.en: His explanation sounded rather {wolly} to me.
e.zh: 他的解释在我听来相当含糊。

e.en: The plant has soft, {wolly} leaves.
e.zh: 这种植物长着柔软的羊毛状叶子。

wolmanizing.t: 沃尔曼法防腐处理木材

e.en: The mill began {wolmanizing} fence posts for outdoor use.
e.zh: 木材厂开始用沃尔曼法处理户外栅栏柱。

e.en: Proper {wolmanizing} helps timber resist decay.
e.zh: 适当的沃尔曼法处理能帮助木材抗腐朽。

e.en: The geologist identified {wolsendorfite} in the uranium ore sample.
e.zh: 地质学家在铀矿样本中鉴定出钼铅铀矿。

e.en: Tiny yellow crystals of {wolsendorfite} lined the old mine specimen.
e.zh: 旧矿石标本上布满了细小的黄色钼铅铀矿晶体。

e.en: The old tale called him a {wolver} of the northern woods.
e.zh: 那个古老故事把他称作北方森林里的狼。

e.en: In the village gossip, the greedy landlord was a {wolver}.
e.zh: 在村里的闲话中，那个贪婪的地主像狼一样狠。

e.en: The trapper wrote {wolverene} in his nineteenth-century journal.
e.zh: 捕兽人在十九世纪的日记里写下了狼獾这个旧拼法。

e.en: A {wolverene} can defend its food fiercely from larger animals.
e.zh: 狼獾能凶猛地保护食物，不让更大的动物靠近。

e.en: A {wolverine} crossed the snowy trail at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时，一只狼獾穿过了积雪的小径。

e.en: The small lawyer fought like a {wolverine} in court.
e.zh: 那位矮个律师在法庭上像狼獾一样凶猛地争辩。

e.en: Several {wolverines} were photographed near the mountain pass.
e.zh: 山口附近拍到了几只狼獾。

e.en: The defenders played like {wolverines} during the final minutes.
e.zh: 最后几分钟里，防守队员们像狼獾一样拼命。

e.en: The novel portrays him as a bitter {woman-hater}.
e.zh: 这部小说把他描写成一个刻薄的厌女者。

e.en: She rejected the label {woman-hater} and defended her record.
e.zh: 她拒绝接受厌女者这个标签，并为自己的履历辩护。

e.en: They had a {woman-to-woman} talk after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后，她们进行了一次女人之间的坦诚谈话。

e.en: Let me speak {woman-to-woman} about the pressure you feel.
e.zh: 让我以女人之间坦诚的方式谈谈你感受到的压力。

e.en: The men ate outside while the {womanfolk} prepared supper.
e.zh: 男人们在外面吃东西，家里的女人们准备晚饭。

e.en: His letters often asked after the {womanfolk} back home.
e.zh: 他的信里常常问候家乡的女眷们。

womanist.t: 女性主义者，尤指黑人女性主义

e.en: She describes herself as a {womanist} scholar.
e.zh: 她自称是一名女性主义学者，尤其关注黑人女性经验。

e.en: The essay uses a {womanist} reading of the novel.
e.zh: 这篇文章用女性主义，特别是黑人女性主义的视角解读小说。

e.en: The poem celebrates her {womanity} without apology.
e.zh: 这首诗毫不掩饰地赞美她的女性特质。

e.en: She felt her {womanity} was judged by narrow social rules.
e.zh: 她觉得自己的女人身份总被狭隘的社会规则评判。

e.en: He continued to {womanize} even after his marriage.
e.zh: 他结婚后仍继续到处追逐女性。

e.en: The director tried to {womanize} the harsh military story.
e.zh: 导演试图给这个冷硬的军事故事加入女性化色彩。

e.en: He had {womanized} for years before settling down.
e.zh: 他安定下来之前，曾多年到处追逐女性。

e.en: The costume was deliberately {womanized} for the stage version.
e.zh: 舞台版服装被有意设计得更女性化。

e.en: Everyone knows he {womanizes} when he travels alone.
e.zh: 大家都知道他独自旅行时会到处追逐女性。

e.en: The adaptation {womanizes} a role originally written for a man.
e.zh: 这个改编把原本为男性写的角色女性化了。

e.en: He spent ten years in a nearly {womanless} mining camp.
e.zh: 他在一个几乎没有女性的采矿营地待了十年。

e.en: The play imagines a {womanless} society run by old generals.
e.zh: 这出戏想象了一个由老将军统治、没有女性的社会。

womanlike.t: 像女人的；有女性气质的

e.en: The statue has a soft, {womanlike} grace.
e.zh: 这座雕像带着柔和的女性般优雅。

e.en: Critics mocked his {womanlike} gestures on stage.
e.zh: 评论者嘲笑他在舞台上像女人一样的手势。

e.en: The campaign celebrated {womanpower} in local politics.
e.zh: 这场运动赞颂地方政治中的女性力量。

e.en: The factory relied on {womanpower} during the war.
e.zh: 战争期间，这家工厂依靠女性劳动力运转。

e.en: The policy promised {womb-to-tomb} health care.
e.zh: 这项政策承诺提供从出生前到死亡的医疗照护。

e.en: Advertisers now track consumers with {womb-to-tomb} ambition.
e.zh: 广告商如今怀着从摇篮前到坟墓都追踪消费者的野心。

e.en: The room felt dark, warm, and strangely {womby}.
e.zh: 这个房间昏暗温暖，奇异地像子宫般包裹人。

e.en: Her installation created a soft, {womby} space for visitors.
e.zh: 她的装置作品为参观者营造出柔软而像子宫般的空间。

e.en: The speech claimed to defend all {womenkind}.
e.zh: 这场演讲声称要捍卫全体女性。

e.en: Old writers sometimes used {womenkind} where we would say women.
e.zh: 旧时作家有时用womenkind来表示我们现在说的女人们。

e.en: The store expanded its {womenswear} section this spring.
e.zh: 这家商店今年春天扩大了女装区。

e.en: She works as a buyer for a {womenswear} brand.
e.zh: 她在一个女装品牌担任采购。

e.en: The museum displayed a carved {womera} beside the spears.
e.zh: 博物馆在长矛旁展出了一件雕刻过的澳洲原住民投矛器。

e.en: He learned how a {womera} increases the force of a throw.
e.zh: 他学习了投矛器如何增强投掷的力量。

e.en: The bass made a heavy {womp} through the wall.
e.zh: 低音穿过墙壁，发出一声沉重的砰响。

e.en: I missed the deadline again, {womp} womp.
e.zh: 我又错过了截止日期，唉，真扫兴。

e.en: The flyer invited all {womyn} to the workshop.
e.zh: 传单邀请所有女性参加这个工作坊，并使用了女权替代拼法。

e.en: Some feminist groups once preferred {womyn} over women.
e.zh: 一些女权团体曾经更喜欢用womyn而不是women。

e.en: I {won't} be late again.
e.zh: 我不会再迟到了。

e.en: The door {won't} open from inside.
e.zh: 这扇门从里面打不开。

e.en: The child stood {wonder-stricken} before the fireworks.
e.zh: 孩子站在烟花前惊叹不已。

e.en: She gave him a {wonder-stricken} look.
e.zh: 她用惊奇的眼神看着他。

e.en: The audience sat {wonder-struck} in silence.
e.zh: 观众惊叹得静静坐着。

e.en: He was {wonder-struck} by the ancient temple.
e.zh: 他被那座古庙震撼得目瞪口呆。

e.en: The villagers called the doctor a {wonder-worker}.
e.zh: 村民们称那位医生为创造奇迹的人。

e.en: In the old tale, the saint was a {wonder-worker}.
e.zh: 在那个古老故事里，这位圣徒是行奇迹的人。

wonder-working.t: 创造奇迹的；神奇有效的

e.en: They praised his {wonder-working} skill.
e.zh: 他们赞叹他那创造奇迹般的技艺。

e.en: The monks believed in a {wonder-working} relic.
e.zh: 修士们相信有一件能显奇迹的圣物。

e.en: The manuscript had {wonderered} written in the margin.
e.zh: 手稿页边写着拼错的wondered。

e.en: She corrected {wonderered} to wondered in the essay.
e.zh: 她把作文里的wonderered改成了wondered。

e.en: The poet described a {wonderous} light.
e.zh: 诗人描写了一道奇妙的光。

e.en: He used the old spelling {wonderous} in his letter.
e.zh: 他在信中用了wonderous这个旧式拼法。

wonderstone.t: 奇石；据称有魔力的石头

e.en: The legend says the {wonderstone} can heal wounds.
e.zh: 传说这块奇石能够治愈伤口。

e.en: She kept a small {wonderstone} on her desk.
e.zh: 她在书桌上放着一块小奇石。

e.en: We were {wonderstruck} by the northern lights.
e.zh: 我们被北极光震撼得惊叹不已。

e.en: The boy looked {wonderstruck} at the huge ship.
e.zh: 男孩望着那艘巨轮，显得目瞪口呆。

e.en: The bridge was considered a {wonderwork} of engineering.
e.zh: 这座桥被认为是工程上的奇迹之作。

e.en: The old hymn celebrates God's {wonderwork}.
e.zh: 那首古老圣歌赞颂上帝的奇妙作为。

wonderworking.t: 创造奇迹的；神奇有效的

e.en: The preacher spoke of a {wonderworking} faith.
e.zh: 传教士谈到一种能创造奇迹的信仰。

e.en: People came seeking her {wonderworking} cure.
e.zh: 人们前来寻求她那神奇有效的疗法。

e.en: The book opens a {wonderworld} for young readers.
e.zh: 这本书为小读者打开了一个奇妙世界。

e.en: The fair felt like a bright {wonderworld}.
e.zh: 那场集市像一个明亮的幻想乐园。

e.en: The hermit would {wone} in the hills.
e.zh: 那位隐士会住在山中。

e.en: Old songs say spirits {wone} by the river.
e.zh: 古老歌谣说精灵栖居在河边。

e.en: He spent all his {wonga} on concert tickets.
e.zh: 他把所有钱都花在了演唱会门票上。

e.en: They needed more {wonga} to finish the trip.
e.zh: 他们需要更多现金才能完成这趟旅行。

e.en: This chair is {wonkier} than the old one.
e.zh: 这把椅子比旧的那把还不稳。

e.en: His second theory sounds even {wonkier}.
e.zh: 他的第二个理论听起来更加怪异。

e.en: The text said I {wonna} go home.
e.zh: 短信里写着I wonna go home这种非标准说法。

e.en: She wrote {wonna} instead of wanna.
e.zh: 她把wanna写成了wonna。

wonned.t: 古语居住；逗留的过去式

e.en: Long ago, shepherds {wonned} on these plains.
e.zh: 很久以前，牧羊人住在这些平原上。

e.en: The tale says a giant {wonned} there.
e.zh: 故事说曾有一个巨人住在那里。

e.en: A {wood-anemone} bloomed beside the path.
e.zh: 一朵林银莲花在小路旁开放。

e.en: The forest floor was covered with {wood-anemones}.
e.zh: 森林地面上开满了林地银莲花。

wood-block.t: 木块；木刻版；木鱼类乐器

e.en: He carved the pattern into a {wood-block}.
e.zh: 他把图案刻进一块木刻版里。

e.en: The percussionist struck the {wood-block} sharply.
e.zh: 打击乐手清脆地敲响了木鱼类乐器。

e.en: The children painted a small {woodhorse} for the playroom.
e.zh: 孩子们给游戏室里的一匹小木马刷了漆。

e.en: The carpenter rested the plank on a sturdy {woodhorse}.
e.zh: 木匠把木板放在结实的木制支架上。

e.en: They restored an old {woodie} with polished side panels.
e.zh: 他们修复了一辆带抛光木质侧板的老式旅行车。

e.en: The wine had a slightly {woodie} smell after aging in oak.
e.zh: 这款酒在橡木桶中陈年后带有一点木头味。

e.en: This trail feels {woodier} than the open coastal path.
e.zh: 这条小径比开阔的海岸路更有林木气息。

e.en: The second sample tasted {woodier} after longer barrel aging.
e.zh: 第二个样品经过更久桶陈后木味更重。

e.en: The {woodiest} part of the garden lies behind the shed.
e.zh: 花园里林木最浓密的地方在棚屋后面。

e.en: That was the {woodiest} whiskey in the tasting flight.
e.zh: 那是这组品鉴酒里木桶味最重的一款。

e.en: The chair's {woodiness} suited the simple kitchen.
e.zh: 这把椅子的木质感很适合那间朴素的厨房。

e.en: Some drinkers dislike the strong {woodiness} of aged spirits.
e.zh: 有些饮酒者不喜欢陈年烈酒里很重的木头味。

e.en: A tired {woodjack} carried his axe back to camp.
e.zh: 疲惫的伐木工扛着斧头回到营地。

e.en: The old book calls the woodpecker a {woodjack}.
e.zh: 那本旧书把啄木鸟称作woodjack。

e.en: A {woodlark} sang from the edge of the pine wood.
e.zh: 一只林百灵在松林边缘鸣唱。

e.en: Birdwatchers came early to hear the shy {woodlark}.
e.zh: 观鸟者一早赶来聆听那种胆小的林百灵。

e.en: Several {woodlarks} nested in the dry grass nearby.
e.zh: 几只林百灵在附近的干草中筑巢。

e.en: The guide could identify {woodlarks} by their soft song.
e.zh: 向导能凭柔和的鸣声辨认林百灵。

e.en: The island looked bare and {woodless} from the boat.
e.zh: 从船上看，那座岛光秃秃的，没有树木。

e.en: A {woodless} design used metal and glass instead.
e.zh: 这个不用木材的设计改用了金属和玻璃。

e.en: His grandfather taught him old {woodlore} during long walks.
e.zh: 祖父在长途散步时教他古老的森林知识。

e.en: Good {woodlore} helps hikers read tracks and weather signs.
e.zh: 扎实的野外知识能帮助徒步者辨认足迹和天气征兆。

e.en: A {woodlouse} curled up under the damp stone.
e.zh: 一只潮虫在潮湿的石头下蜷成一团。

e.en: Children watched the {woodlouse} crawl across the log.
e.zh: 孩子们看着那只鼠妇爬过木头。

e.en: A clear {woodnote} rose from the trees at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时分，树林里传来清亮的鸟鸣。

e.en: The poet loved every wild {woodnote} in spring.
e.zh: 诗人喜爱春天里每一种自然的林间乐音。

e.en: Soft {woodnotes} drifted across the quiet meadow.
e.zh: 轻柔的林中鸟鸣飘过安静的草地。

e.en: Her song tried to imitate the {woodnotes} of morning.
e.zh: 她的歌试图模仿清晨自然的林间乐音。

e.en: The farmer called the spotted woodpecker a {woodpie}.
e.zh: 农夫把那只斑点啄木鸟称作woodpie。

e.en: In old dialect, a {woodpie} might mean a woodpecker.
e.zh: 在旧方言中，woodpie可以指啄木鸟。

e.en: The museum displayed a delicate Japanese {woodprint}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一幅精美的日本木版画。

e.en: She chose a {woodprint} fabric for the cushions.
e.zh: 她为靠垫选了一种木纹印花布料。

e.en: The {woodranger} checked the boundary after the storm.
e.zh: 风暴过后，护林员检查了林地边界。

e.en: A local {woodranger} guided visitors through the reserve.
e.zh: 当地一名林地巡守带游客穿过保护区。

e.en: The collector labeled the tiny crystal as {woodruffite}.
e.zh: 收藏者把那颗小晶体标注为伍德拉夫矿。

e.en: Few museums have a clear specimen of {woodruffite}.
e.zh: 很少有博物馆藏有清晰的伍德拉夫矿标本。

e.en: Use a long {woodscrew} to fasten the hinge securely.
e.zh: 用一枚长木螺钉把铰链牢牢固定住。

e.en: The old {woodscrew} snapped inside the cabinet door.
e.zh: 那枚旧木螺丝断在柜门里面了。

e.en: The cabin's {woodsiness} made it feel far from town.
e.zh: 小屋的林木气息让人觉得它远离城镇。

e.en: She liked the {woodsiness} of the cedar-scented soap.
e.zh: 她喜欢那块雪松香皂带来的树林感。

e.en: The craftsman sanded the rough {woodskin} before staining.
e.zh: 工匠在上色前打磨了粗糙的木材外层。

e.en: Thin {woodskin} peeled away from the weathered post.
e.zh: 风化柱子上薄薄的木表皮剥落下来。

e.en: The pendant was carved from polished {woodstone}.
e.zh: 这个吊坠是用抛光木化石雕成的。

e.en: The architect chose {woodstone} tiles for a natural look.
e.zh: 建筑师选用仿木石材瓷砖来营造自然效果。

e.en: The old beams showed signs of {wood-boring} insects.
e.zh: 这些旧梁上有蛀木昆虫活动的痕迹。

e.en: A {wood-boring} tool can make clean holes in hardwood.
e.zh: 钻木工具能在硬木上打出整齐的孔。

e.en: The {wood-carver} shaped the figure by hand.
e.zh: 木雕师用手工雕出了这个人物。

e.en: She bought a small owl from a local {wood-carver}.
e.zh: 她从当地木刻匠那里买了一只小猫头鹰木雕。

e.en: A sharp {wood-chip} stuck to his sleeve.
e.zh: 一片尖木屑粘在了他的袖子上。

e.en: The garden path was covered with {wood-chip}.
e.zh: 花园小路上铺着木片。

e.en: The {wood-cutter} carried his axe into the forest.
e.zh: 伐木工带着斧头走进森林。

e.en: In the story, a poor {wood-cutter} finds a hidden bag of gold.
e.zh: 故事里，一个贫穷的砍柴人发现了一袋藏起来的金子。

e.en: A {wood-louse} crawled out from under the flowerpot.
e.zh: 一只潮虫从花盆底下爬了出来。

e.en: Children watched the {wood-louse} curl into a tiny ball.
e.zh: 孩子们看着那只鼠妇蜷成一个小球。

e.en: They met in a {wood-paneled} conference room.
e.zh: 他们在一间镶木板的会议室里见面。

e.en: The old library had dark, {wood-paneled} walls.
e.zh: 那座老图书馆有深色木饰面墙壁。

e.en: A {wood-rat} built its nest beside the shed.
e.zh: 一只林鼠在棚屋旁边筑了巢。

e.en: The biologist trapped a {wood-rat} for a health study.
e.zh: 生物学家捕获了一只木鼠用于健康研究。

e.en: Use a {wood-screw} to fasten the hinge.
e.zh: 用木螺钉把铰链固定住。

e.en: The loose shelf needed one longer {wood-screw}.
e.zh: 这块松动的架板需要一颗更长的木螺丝。

e.en: The smell of {wood-smoke} filled the cabin.
e.zh: 小屋里充满了柴烟的味道。

e.en: A line of {wood-smoke} rose above the village.
e.zh: 一缕柴烟从村子上空升起。

e.en: The vase was packed in {wood-wool} for shipping.
e.zh: 花瓶用木丝包好后寄出。

e.en: Farmers sometimes use {wood-wool} as bedding for animals.
e.zh: 农民有时用刨花填料给牲畜铺垫。

e.en: He filled the {woodbin} before the storm arrived.
e.zh: 暴风雨来临前，他把木柴箱装满了。

e.en: A brass-handled {woodbin} stood beside the fireplace.
e.zh: 壁炉旁放着一个带黄铜把手的柴筐。

e.en: The hedge was tangled with {woodbind} in summer.
e.zh: 夏天，树篱上缠满了忍冬藤。

e.en: Old poems often mention {woodbind} climbing over cottage walls.
e.zh: 古诗中常写到忍冬攀上乡间小屋的墙。

e.en: The carpenter found a {woodborer} inside the beam.
e.zh: 木匠在梁里发现了一只蛀木虫。

e.en: This spray helps protect furniture from {woodborer} damage.
e.zh: 这种喷剂有助于保护家具免受蛀木昆虫破坏。

e.en: A {woodcarved} angel hung above the doorway.
e.zh: 门口上方挂着一个木雕天使。

e.en: The museum displayed several {woodcarved} masks.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了几件木刻面具。

e.en: A {woodchat} perched on the thorn bush.
e.zh: 一只红背伯劳类小鸟停在荆棘丛上。

e.en: The guide identified the {woodchat} by its black eye stripe.
e.zh: 向导凭它黑色的眼纹认出了那只红背伯劳。

e.en: A single {woodchip} landed in his coffee.
e.zh: 一片木屑落进了他的咖啡里。

e.en: The playground surface is made of soft {woodchip}.
e.zh: 游乐场地面铺的是柔软的木片。

e.en: They spread {woodchips} around the young trees.
e.zh: 他们在小树周围铺上木片。

e.en: The saw left {woodchips} all over the floor.
e.zh: 锯子把木屑弄得到处都是。

e.en: The {woodchopper} worked until dusk.
e.zh: 劈柴人一直干到黄昏。

e.en: A noisy {woodchopper} stood behind the barn.
e.zh: 谷仓后面放着一台吵闹的砍木机。

e.en: The {woodcreeper} moved quickly up the tree trunk.
e.zh: 那只旋木雀类鸟很快沿着树干往上爬。

e.en: Birdwatchers heard a {woodcreeper} calling in the forest.
e.zh: 观鸟者听见林中有爬树鸟在鸣叫。

e.en: His {wooden-headed} refusal delayed the whole project.
e.zh: 他死脑筋的拒绝拖慢了整个项目。

e.en: Only a {wooden-headed} official would ignore such clear evidence.
e.zh: 只有愚钝的官员才会无视这么清楚的证据。

e.en: Don't be a {woodenhead}; read the instructions first.
e.zh: 别当笨蛋，先读说明。

e.en: The comic character is a lovable {woodenhead}.
e.zh: 这个喜剧角色是个讨人喜欢的木头脑袋。

e.en: That was a {woodenheaded} answer to a simple question.
e.zh: 对这么简单的问题，那是个愚笨的回答。

e.en: She grew tired of his {woodenheaded} stubbornness.
e.zh: 她受够了他那木头脑袋般的固执。

e.en: The sergeant called the recruit a {woodentop}.
e.zh: 中士把那个新兵叫作木头脑袋。

e.en: In old slang, a {woodentop} was a stupid person.
e.zh: 在旧俚语里，woodentop 指傻瓜。

e.en: The market stall sold bowls and other {woodenware}.
e.zh: 市场摊位出售碗和其他木制器皿。

e.en: Traditional {woodenware} should be dried carefully after washing.
e.zh: 传统木器清洗后要仔细晾干。

e.en: The table's {woodgrain} looked beautiful in the morning light.
e.zh: 晨光下，桌子的木纹显得很漂亮。

e.en: He chose a {woodgrain} finish for the plastic dashboard.
e.zh: 他给塑料仪表板选了仿木纹饰面。

e.en: The {woodturner} shaped the bowl on a lathe.
e.zh: 木旋工在车床上把木碗加工成形。

e.en: A skilled {woodturner} can make table legs identical.
e.zh: 熟练的木车床工匠能做出完全一样的桌腿。

e.en: The shop sells handmade {woodware} for kitchens.
e.zh: 这家店出售厨房用的手工木制器皿。

e.en: Old {woodware} needs careful cleaning and oiling.
e.zh: 旧木器需要仔细清洁并上油保养。

e.en: Trucks delivered fresh logs to the {woodyard}.
e.zh: 卡车把新砍的原木运到木材堆场。

e.en: He bought winter fuel from a local {woodyard}.
e.zh: 他从当地柴场购买过冬燃料。

e.en: Her persistent {wooer} sent flowers every Friday.
e.zh: 那位执着的追求者每周五都给她送花。

e.en: In the old poem, the {wooer} speaks formally.
e.zh: 在那首古诗里，求爱者说话很正式。

e.en: Several {wooers} waited outside her father's house.
e.zh: 几位求爱者等在她父亲家门外。

e.en: The company attracted many eager {wooers}.
e.zh: 这家公司吸引了许多热切的追求者。

e.en: He regretted using {woofter} as an insult.
e.zh: 他后悔把“男同性恋者”这个贬称当作侮辱。

e.en: The old novel includes the slur {woofter}.
e.zh: 那本旧小说里出现了“woofter”这个歧视性称呼。

e.en: The puppy made a soft {woofy} sound.
e.zh: 小狗发出一声轻轻的汪汪声。

e.en: The speakers had a muddy, {woofy} bass.
e.zh: 这些音箱的低音浑浊而轰隆隆。

e.en: A {wook} asked for a ride after the concert.
e.zh: 演唱会后，一个邋遢的流浪乐迷请求搭车。

e.en: The festival campsite was full of cheerful {wooks}.
e.zh: 音乐节营地里到处是开心的嬉皮流浪者。

e.en: Sailors {woold} the mast with heavy rope.
e.zh: 水手们用粗绳缠绕桅杆来加固。

e.en: They {woold} the cracked spar before sailing.
e.zh: 出航前，他们把裂开的帆桁缠绳加固。

e.en: The {woolder} tightened the rope around the mast.
e.zh: 缠索工把桅杆周围的绳索勒紧。

e.en: A careful {woolder} could save a damaged spar.
e.zh: 细心的缠索工能救回一根受损的帆桁。

e.en: The crew began {woolding} the weakened mast.
e.zh: 船员开始给变弱的桅杆缠索加固。

e.en: Old manuals describe {woolding} in careful detail.
e.zh: 旧手册详细描述了缠索加固的方法。

e.en: The dress was made of cheap {woolenet}.
e.zh: 这条连衣裙是用廉价仿毛织物做的。

e.en: Merchants advertised {woolenet} as a practical fabric.
e.zh: 商人把薄毛料宣传成实用面料。

e.en: She chose {woolenette} for the children's coats.
e.zh: 她选了仿毛织物来做孩子们的外套。

e.en: The catalog listed {woolenette} beside cotton blends.
e.zh: 目录把轻薄毛料列在棉混纺旁边。

e.en: The tanner bought a fresh {woolfell}.
e.zh: 制革工买了一张新鲜的带毛羊皮。

e.en: A {woolfell} was stretched near the shed.
e.zh: 一张带羊毛的羊皮被撑开放在棚屋旁。

e.en: Don't {woolgather} while the machine is running.
e.zh: 机器运转时不要走神。

e.en: He would {woolgather} through long afternoon meetings.
e.zh: 漫长的下午会议里，他常常胡思乱想。

e.en: The teacher called him a hopeless {woolgatherer}.
e.zh: 老师说他是个无可救药的爱走神的人。

e.en: A dreamy {woolgatherer} may notice unusual details.
e.zh: 爱空想的人也许会注意到不寻常的细节。

e.en: Her {woolgathering} made her miss the question.
e.zh: 她一走神，就错过了那个问题。

e.en: The essay dismisses such plans as {woolgathering}.
e.zh: 这篇文章把这类计划斥为空想。

woolgrower.t: 养羊产毛者；羊毛生产者

e.en: The {woolgrower} worried about falling fleece prices.
e.zh: 这位羊毛生产者担心羊毛价格下跌。

e.en: A successful {woolgrower} needs healthy sheep and pasture.
e.zh: 成功的养羊产毛者需要健康的羊和牧场。

woolhat.t: 乡下人；南方穷白人的贬称

e.en: The politician used {woolhat} to mock rural voters.
e.zh: 那名政客用“乡下人”这个贬称嘲笑农村选民。

e.en: In the memoir, {woolhat} appears as dated slang.
e.zh: 在那本回忆录中，“woolhat”是过时的俚语。

e.en: The tailor recommended {woollenette} for a light coat.
e.zh: 裁缝推荐用轻薄毛料做一件薄外套。

e.en: Old advertisements praised {woollenette} as warm and cheap.
e.zh: 旧广告称赞仿毛织物既暖和又便宜。

woollenize.t: 使像毛织物；作毛化处理

e.en: The mill tried to {woollenize} the cotton blend.
e.zh: 工厂试图把这种棉混纺做成像毛织物一样。

e.en: Chemicals can {woollenize} fibers for a softer feel.
e.zh: 化学处理能让纤维毛化，手感更柔软。

e.en: The {woolliest} blanket stayed on the sofa.
e.zh: 最毛茸茸的毯子一直放在沙发上。

e.en: That was the {woolliest} argument in the report.
e.zh: 那是报告里最含混的论点。

e.en: The caterpillar moved {woollily} across the leaf.
e.zh: 毛茸茸的毛虫在叶子上爬过去。

e.en: He answered {woollily}, avoiding every clear detail.
e.zh: 他回答得含含糊糊，避开了所有明确细节。

e.en: After the second injection, she felt {woozier} than before.
e.zh: 打完第二针后，她觉得比之前更头晕。

e.en: The stale air made him even {woozier} during the meeting.
e.zh: 污浊的空气让他在会议中更加昏沉。

e.en: I felt {wooziest} when I stood up too quickly.
e.zh: 我起身太快时感觉最头晕。

e.en: That was the {wooziest} morning after my long flight.
e.zh: 长途飞行后那个早晨是我最昏沉的时候。

e.en: The medicine may cause mild {wooziness} at first.
e.zh: 这种药一开始可能会引起轻微头晕。

e.en: Her {wooziness} faded after she drank some water.
e.zh: 她喝了些水后，昏沉感慢慢消退了。

e.en: In the dialect, {wor} means our family or our people.
e.zh: 在这种方言里，wor表示我们的家人或咱们的人。

e.en: He called his sister {wor} lass in a local accent.
e.zh: 他带着地方口音把妹妹称作“咱家的姑娘”。

e.en: The teacher helped a {word-blind} child read aloud.
e.zh: 老师帮助一个有阅读障碍的孩子朗读。

e.en: Older doctors sometimes called dyslexic patients {word-blind}.
e.zh: 早期医生有时把诵读困难患者称为word-blind。

e.en: She copied new terms into her {word-book} every night.
e.zh: 她每天晚上把新词抄进自己的词汇本。

e.en: The old {word-book} gave several spellings for the same term.
e.zh: 那本旧字典为同一个词列出了几种拼写。

e.en: The software detects each {word-boundary} before counting tokens.
e.zh: 软件在统计词元前会检测每个词边界。

e.en: Children learn that spaces mark a {word-boundary} in English.
e.zh: 孩子们会学到英语中的空格表示单词分界。

e.en: The course uses {word-building} games to teach prefixes.
e.zh: 这门课用构词游戏来教授前缀。

e.en: Regular reading is useful for {word-building} in a second language.
e.zh: 经常阅读有助于第二语言的词汇扩展。

e.en: A noun and a verb belong to different {word-class} groups.
e.zh: 名词和动词属于不同的词类。

e.en: Students marked the {word-class} of each item in the sentence.
e.zh: 学生标出了句中每个项目的词性类别。

e.en: A {word-deaf} patient may hear sounds but not understand speech.
e.zh: 词聋患者可能听得到声音，却听不懂话语。

e.en: The article used {word-deaf} as an older medical term.
e.zh: 那篇文章把word-deaf作为较早的医学术语使用。

e.en: She translated the poem {word-for-word}, losing its rhythm.
e.zh: 她逐字翻译了那首诗，结果失去了韵律。

e.en: He repeated the warning {word-for-word} in court.
e.zh: 他在法庭上一字不差地重复了那句警告。

e.en: Suffixes play a major role in English {word-formation}.
e.zh: 后缀在英语构词法中起着重要作用。

e.en: The chapter explains {word-formation} through compounds and blends.
e.zh: 这一章通过复合词和混成词解释词语形成。

e.en: We played a {word-game} during the long train ride.
e.zh: 长途火车途中，我们玩了一个文字游戏。

e.en: The headline is a clever {word-game} on the actor's name.
e.zh: 这个标题巧妙地拿演员的名字做了词语游戏。

e.en: Reading poetry enriched her private {word-hoard}.
e.zh: 阅读诗歌丰富了她个人的词汇储备。

e.en: Old English writers used {word-hoard} to mean a store of words.
e.zh: 古英语作家用word-hoard表示词语的储藏。

e.en: The teacher gave us a {word-list} for Friday's test.
e.zh: 老师给了我们一份周五考试用的单词表。

e.en: Add unfamiliar terms to your {word-list} as you read.
e.zh: 阅读时把不熟悉的词加入你的词汇清单。

e.en: The restaurant became popular through {word-of-mouth}.
e.zh: 这家餐馆靠口口相传变得受欢迎。

e.en: Most new clients arrive by {word-of-mouth} recommendations.
e.zh: 大多数新客户都是通过口碑推荐来的。

e.en: The critic called Dickens a vivid {word-painter}.
e.zh: 评论家称狄更斯是善于用文字描绘的作家。

e.en: A good {word-painter} can make a street feel alive.
e.zh: 优秀的文字描绘者能让一条街显得鲜活。

e.en: Her {word-painting} of the storm filled the page with motion.
e.zh: 她对暴风雨的文字描绘让整页都充满动感。

e.en: The essay relies on {word-painting} rather than argument.
e.zh: 这篇文章主要依靠生动描写，而不是论证。

word-perfect.t: 一字不差的；背得滚瓜烂熟的

e.en: By opening night, every actor was {word-perfect}.
e.zh: 到首演当晚，每个演员都把台词背得一字不差。

e.en: She gave a {word-perfect} account of the conversation.
e.zh: 她一字不差地复述了那次谈话。

e.en: The memoir opens with a sharp {word-picture} of village life.
e.zh: 这本回忆录开头用鲜明的文字画面描写乡村生活。

e.en: His {word-picture} made the missing room easy to imagine.
e.zh: 他的文字描写让那个消失的房间很容易想象。

word-processor.t: 文字处理器；文字处理软件

e.en: She wrote the report in a basic {word-processor}.
e.zh: 她用一个基础文字处理软件写了报告。

e.en: An old {word-processor} sat beside the printer.
e.zh: 打印机旁边放着一台老式文字处理器。

e.en: The speech was full of {word-spinning} but little policy.
e.zh: 这篇演讲满是辞藻堆砌，却几乎没有政策内容。

e.en: He admired her {word-spinning} in the comic verse.
e.zh: 他欣赏她在滑稽诗中玩弄文字的技巧。

e.en: The debate turned into legal {word-splitting} over one phrase.
e.zh: 这场辩论变成了围绕一个短语的法律咬文嚼字。

e.en: The parser uses {word-splitting} to separate compounds.
e.zh: 解析器使用词语拆分来分开复合词。

e.en: The {woolliness} of the blanket made it feel warm.
e.zh: 这条毯子毛茸茸的，摸起来很暖。

e.en: The report's {woolliness} confused the whole team.
e.zh: 报告写得含糊混乱，让整个团队都困惑。

woolly-headed.t: 头脑糊涂的；想法混乱的

e.en: His {woolly-headed} plan ignored the main problem.
e.zh: 他那个头脑糊涂的计划忽视了主要问题。

e.en: She sounded {woolly-headed} after the long flight.
e.zh: 长途飞行后，她听起来有些糊里糊涂。

e.en: The proposal was too {woolly-minded} to approve.
e.zh: 这份提案思路太混乱，无法批准。

e.en: He becomes {woolly-minded} when he is tired.
e.zh: 他一累就会变得思维不清。

e.en: The {woolman} inspected every fleece before buying it.
e.zh: 那名羊毛商在购买前检查了每张羊毛。

e.en: A retired {woolman} taught us how wool was sorted.
e.zh: 一位退休羊毛工人教我们羊毛是怎样分拣的。

e.en: The {woolmen} met at the market before dawn.
e.zh: 那些羊毛商在黎明前就在市场碰面。

e.en: Experienced {woolmen} could judge quality by touch.
e.zh: 有经验的羊毛工人靠手感就能判断品质。

e.en: He lifted the heavy {woolpack} onto the cart.
e.zh: 他把沉重的羊毛包搬上了马车。

e.en: The old inn was named after a {woolpack}.
e.zh: 那家老客栈以羊毛包命名。

e.en: Several {woolpacks} were stacked by the barn door.
e.zh: 几包羊毛堆在谷仓门旁。

e.en: The ship carried {woolpacks} from the southern farms.
e.zh: 那艘船运载着南方农场来的羊毛包。

woolsack.t: 羊毛袋；英国上议院议长座

e.en: The farmer dragged a {woolsack} across the yard.
e.zh: 农夫拖着一个羊毛袋穿过院子。

e.en: The Lord Speaker sits on the {Woolsack}.
e.zh: 英国上议院议长坐在羊毛袋座上。

e.en: The shearers gathered in the {woolshed} at sunrise.
e.zh: 剪羊毛工人在日出时聚到剪羊毛棚里。

e.en: Rain drummed loudly on the tin {woolshed} roof.
e.zh: 雨点重重敲打着羊毛棚的铁皮屋顶。

e.en: A soft {woolskin} lay beside the fireplace.
e.zh: 壁炉旁铺着一张柔软的带毛羊皮。

e.en: The trader sold {woolskin} for warm winter coats.
e.zh: 商人出售羊毛皮，用来做保暖冬衣。

e.en: The {woolsorter} separated fine fleece from coarse wool.
e.zh: 羊毛分拣工把细羊毛和粗羊毛分开。

e.en: My grandfather worked as a {woolsorter} in Yorkshire.
e.zh: 我祖父曾在约克郡当羊毛分拣工。

e.en: Her framed {woolwork} showed a bright garden scene.
e.zh: 她装框的毛线刺绣描绘了一处明亮的花园景色。

e.en: The museum displayed Victorian {woolwork} and lace.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了维多利亚时期的羊毛制品和蕾丝。

wooly-headed.t: 头脑糊涂的；想法混乱的

e.en: That {wooly-headed} answer did not satisfy the judge.
e.zh: 那个糊里糊涂的回答没有让法官满意。

e.en: I get {wooly-headed} when I skip lunch.
e.zh: 我不吃午饭时脑子就会发蒙。

e.en: The hunter used a {woomera} to throw the spear farther.
e.zh: 猎人用投矛器把长矛投得更远。

e.en: A carved {woomera} was displayed in the museum.
e.zh: 博物馆里展出了一件雕刻过的澳洲投矛板。

e.en: The chorus needs more {woomph} to excite the crowd.
e.zh: 副歌需要更有冲劲，才能点燃观众。

e.en: The engine started with a deep {woomph}.
e.zh: 发动机轰的一声低沉地启动了。

e.en: The resort advertised luxury packages for {woopies}.
e.zh: 度假村向富裕退休族宣传豪华套餐。

e.en: Some newspapers called the new retirees {woopies}.
e.zh: 一些报纸把这些新退休的富裕老人称作woopies。

e.en: {Woops}, I sent the message to the wrong group.
e.zh: 哎呀，我把消息发错群了。

e.en: She said {woops} after spilling coffee on the notes.
e.zh: 她把咖啡洒在笔记上后说了声糟了。

e.en: The explorer wrote about {woorali} in his journal.
e.zh: 探险家在日记中写到了南美箭毒。

e.en: Some tribes used {woorali} on hunting arrows.
e.zh: 一些部族把箭毒涂在狩猎用箭上。

e.en: The train passed with a sudden {woosh}.
e.zh: 火车嗖的一声突然驶过。

e.en: Cold air seemed to {woosh} through the open door.
e.zh: 冷空气似乎从敞开的门里呼地灌进来。

e.en: A cyclist {wooshed} past us on the hill.
e.zh: 一名骑车人从山坡上嗖地超过了我们。

e.en: The doors opened and air {wooshed} into the tunnel.
e.zh: 门一打开，空气呼地涌进隧道。

e.en: The rocket {wooshes} upward in a cloud of smoke.
e.zh: 火箭在烟雾中呼啸着升空。

e.en: We heard several {wooshes} from the fireworks outside.
e.zh: 我们听见外面的烟花发出几声嗖嗖声。

e.en: Water was {wooshing} through the narrow pipe.
e.zh: 水正哗地从狭窄的管道里冲过。

e.en: The {wooshing} sound grew louder as the train approached.
e.zh: 火车靠近时，那种呼啸声越来越响。

e.en: {Woot}, we finally fixed the bug before midnight.
e.zh: 太棒了，我们终于在午夜前修好了这个漏洞。

e.en: The chat filled with {woot} after the team scored.
e.zh: 球队得分后，聊天区里满是欢呼。

e.en: The blade was forged from ancient {wootz} steel.
e.zh: 这把刀是用古代乌兹钢锻造的。

e.en: Researchers studied {wootz} to understand Damascus steel.
e.zh: 研究人员研究乌兹钢，以了解大马士革钢。

e.en: She copied new vocabulary into her {wordbook}.
e.zh: 她把新词汇抄进自己的单词本。

e.en: The old {wordbook} listed local dialect terms.
e.zh: 那本旧词汇表收录了当地的方言词。

e.en: This is the {wordiest} paragraph in the report.
e.zh: 这是报告里最冗长的一段。

e.en: Among all the speakers, Marta was the {wordiest}.
e.zh: 在所有发言者中，玛塔说得最啰嗦。

e.en: The policy was {wordily} explained in five pages.
e.zh: 这项政策被啰啰嗦嗦地解释了五页。

e.en: He answered {wordily} when a simple yes would do.
e.zh: 明明简单回答是就够了，他却说得很冗长。

e.en: The editor reduced the essay's {wordiness}.
e.zh: 编辑减少了这篇文章的啰嗦之处。

e.en: Legal {wordiness} can confuse ordinary readers.
e.zh: 法律文本的冗长措辞会让普通读者困惑。

e.en: The child made a {wordish} sound while pointing.
e.zh: 孩子一边指着东西，一边发出像词一样的声音。

e.en: The poem uses strange, {wordish} fragments.
e.zh: 这首诗用了奇怪的、近似词语的片段。

wordmonger.t: 卖弄词藻的人；玩弄文字者

e.en: The critic dismissed him as a {wordmonger}.
e.zh: 评论家把他贬为一个卖弄词藻的人。

e.en: A clever {wordmonger} can still write empty prose.
e.zh: 会玩弄文字的人也可能写出空洞的文章。

e.en: The speech was full of political {wordmongering}.
e.zh: 这场演讲充满了政治性的文字游戏。

e.en: She prefers plain language to academic {wordmongering}.
e.zh: 比起学术式的卖弄词藻，她更喜欢直白语言。

e.en: We did a {wordsearch} after lunch.
e.zh: 午饭后我们玩了一个找词游戏。

e.en: The app includes a fast {wordsearch} tool.
e.zh: 这个应用包含一个快速的单词搜索工具。

e.en: Her essays show impressive {wordsmanship}.
e.zh: 她的文章显示出令人印象深刻的文字功夫。

e.en: Good {wordsmanship} cannot hide weak ideas.
e.zh: 再好的遣词技巧也掩盖不了薄弱的观点。

e.en: Turn on {wordwrap} before editing the file.
e.zh: 编辑文件前先打开自动换行。

e.en: Poor {wordwrap} made the paragraph hard to read.
e.zh: 糟糕的文字换行让这段话很难阅读。

e.en: Each mechanic filled out a {work-card}.
e.zh: 每名机械工都填写了一张工作卡。

e.en: The manager checked the {work-card} for overtime hours.
e.zh: 经理查看工时记录卡上的加班时间。

e.en: Her {work-experiences} helped her choose a career.
e.zh: 她的工作经历帮助她选择了职业方向。

e.en: Students discussed their summer {work-experiences} in class.
e.zh: 学生们在课堂上讨论了暑期职场体验。

e.en: The factory needs a larger {work-force}.
e.zh: 这家工厂需要更多劳动力。

e.en: A skilled {work-force} attracts new investment.
e.zh: 熟练的员工队伍会吸引新的投资。

e.en: The tunnel crew reached the {work-head} by dawn.
e.zh: 隧道施工队在黎明前到达了施工面。

e.en: Supplies were carried forward to the {work-head}.
e.zh: 物资被运送到前方的工作端头。

work-horse.t: 吃苦耐劳的人；主力设备

e.en: Tom is the team's reliable {work-horse}.
e.zh: 汤姆是团队里可靠的苦干者。

e.en: This old printer is still our office {work-horse}.
e.zh: 这台旧打印机仍是办公室里的主力设备。

work-in.t: 插入安排；现场抗议活动

e.en: The salon accepted one {work-in} before closing.
e.zh: 沙龙在关门前临时插入安排了一位客人。

e.en: Students organized a {work-in} at the library.
e.zh: 学生们在图书馆组织了一场现场抗议活动。

e.en: The accountant valued the {work-in-process} inventory.
e.zh: 会计评估了在制品库存的价值。

e.en: This report is still {work-in-process}.
e.zh: 这份报告仍在进行中。

work-in-progress.t: 未完成作品；进行中的工作

e.en: The painting is a {work-in-progress}.
e.zh: 这幅画还是一件未完成作品。

e.en: Our hiring plan remains a {work-in-progress}.
e.zh: 我们的招聘计划仍在推进和完善中。

work-ins.t: 插入安排；现场抗议活动

e.en: The clinic allowed two {work-ins} that morning.
e.zh: 诊所那天上午允许了两次临时插入安排。

e.en: The union planned several {work-ins} across campus.
e.zh: 工会计划在校园各处举行几场现场抗议活动。

e.en: Her {workload} doubled after the manager resigned.
e.zh: 经理辞职后，她的工作量翻了一倍。

e.en: We need to reduce the team's {workload}.
e.zh: 我们需要减少团队的工作量。

e.en: I had lunch with a {workmate} today.
e.zh: 我今天和一位同事一起吃了午饭。

e.en: His old {workmate} helped him find another job.
e.zh: 他的老工友帮他找到了另一份工作。

e.en: She does a short {workout} every morning.
e.zh: 她每天早上做一次短时间锻炼。

e.en: Can you {work out} the total cost?
e.zh: 你能算出总费用吗？

e.en: Safety rules are strict in this {workplace}.
e.zh: 这个工作场所的安全规定很严格。

e.en: Many people want a more flexible {workplace}.
e.zh: 许多人希望有更灵活的工作场所。

e.en: The teacher gave us a grammar {worksheet}.
e.zh: 老师给了我们一张语法练习题纸。

e.en: Enter the figures on the first {worksheet}.
e.zh: 把这些数字填在第一张工作表里。

e.en: The bicycle was repaired in a small {workshop}.
e.zh: 自行车是在一个小车间里修好的。

e.en: She attended a writing {workshop} last weekend.
e.zh: 她上周末参加了一个写作研讨会。

e.en: He called his cousin {work-shy} and unreliable.
e.zh: 他称自己的表弟怕干活，而且不可靠。

e.en: The article mocked supposedly {work-shy} young people.
e.zh: 那篇文章嘲笑所谓懒于工作的年轻人。

e.en: He came home in {work-soiled} clothes.
e.zh: 他穿着干活弄脏的衣服回到家。

e.en: Her {work-soiled} hands showed a long day in the garden.
e.zh: 她那双劳动弄脏的手说明她在花园里忙了一整天。

e.en: She paid tuition through a {work-study} program.
e.zh: 她通过勤工俭学项目支付学费。

e.en: His {work-study} schedule left little free time.
e.zh: 他的半工半读安排让他几乎没有空闲时间。

e.en: The drivers began a {work-to-rule} protest on Monday.
e.zh: 司机们周一开始了按章怠工的抗议。

e.en: A {work-to-rule} can slow an airport without a strike.
e.zh: 按章怠工不用罢工也能让机场运转变慢。

e.en: Wipe the {worktop} after cutting raw meat.
e.zh: 切完生肉后要擦干净厨房操作台面。

e.en: They chose a stone {worktop} for the new kitchen.
e.zh: 他们为新厨房选了石质操作台面。

e.en: The speaker tried to {work up} the crowd.
e.zh: 演讲者试图把人群的情绪调动起来。

e.en: The doctor ordered a full {workup} before surgery.
e.zh: 医生要求手术前做一次全面检查。

e.en: The plan was {workably} simple for a small team.
e.zh: 这个计划简单可行，适合小团队执行。

e.en: They arranged the shifts {workably} despite staff shortages.
e.zh: 尽管人手不足，他们还是把班次安排得可以运转。

e.en: The cheaper tool is a {workalike} of the original.
e.zh: 这个更便宜的工具是原版的功能相似替代品。

e.en: Several {workalike} programs can open the same files.
e.zh: 几个工作方式相似的程序都能打开这些文件。

workaround.t: 变通办法；临时解决方案

e.en: We found a {workaround} for the software bug.
e.zh: 我们找到了绕过这个软件漏洞的变通办法。

e.en: This {workaround} is useful but not permanent.
e.zh: 这个临时解决方案有用，但不是长久之计。

e.en: She kept her needles in a small {workbag}.
e.zh: 她把针放在一个小针线活袋里。

e.en: The mechanic carried a heavy {workbag} to the van.
e.zh: 修理工把一个沉重的工具袋拎到货车旁。

e.en: Grandmother put the torn socks in her {workbasket}.
e.zh: 祖母把破袜子放进她的针线篮里。

e.en: The editor's {workbasket} was full of urgent requests.
e.zh: 编辑的工作篮里堆满了紧急请求。

e.en: Clamp the wood firmly to the {workboard}.
e.zh: 把木料牢牢夹在工作板上。

e.en: The team moved each task across the {workboard}.
e.zh: 团队把每项任务在作业看板上逐步移动。

e.en: He opened his {workbox} and took out a chisel.
e.zh: 他打开工具箱，取出一把凿子。

e.en: Her sewing {workbox} sat beside the chair.
e.zh: 她的针线盒放在椅子旁边。

e.en: The old text spells work as {worke}.
e.zh: 这篇古文把 work 拼作 worke。

e.en: In the manuscript, {worke} appears several times.
e.zh: 在这份手稿中，worke 出现了好几次。

e.en: The factory promoted him as a {worker-cadre}.
e.zh: 工厂提拔他为工人干部。

e.en: A {worker-cadre} often linked management with the shop floor.
e.zh: 工人干部常常在管理层和车间之间起联系作用。

e.en: The union nominated a {worker-director} to the board.
e.zh: 工会提名一名职工董事进入董事会。

e.en: A {worker-director} can represent employees in company decisions.
e.zh: 职工董事可以在公司决策中代表员工。

e.en: The {worker-directors} voted against the closure.
e.zh: 职工董事们投票反对关闭工厂。

e.en: Two {worker-directors} joined the board last year.
e.zh: 去年有两名职工董事加入董事会。

e.en: He trained as a {worker-engineer} in the steel plant.
e.zh: 他在钢铁厂受训，成为工人出身的工程师。

e.en: The novel praises the practical skill of a {worker-engineer}.
e.zh: 这部小说赞扬了一名工人出身工程师的实践技能。

e.en: The poster used strong {worker-peasant} imagery.
e.zh: 那张海报使用了强烈的工农形象。

e.en: The policy claimed to serve the {worker-peasant} alliance.
e.zh: 这项政策声称服务于工农联盟。

e.en: The poster praised the {worker-peasant-soldier} alliance.
e.zh: 那张海报赞颂工农兵联盟。

e.en: She studied a {worker-peasant-soldier} drama from the 1970s.
e.zh: 她研究了一部二十世纪七十年代的工农兵戏剧。

e.en: The college offers evening courses for {worker-students}.
e.zh: 这所学院为半工半读学生开设夜校课程。

e.en: As a {worker-student}, he divided his week between shifts and lectures.
e.zh: 作为工读生，他一周里要兼顾上班和听课。

worker-teacher.t: 工人教师；兼做教学的工人

e.en: The program trained experienced mechanics as {worker-teachers}.
e.zh: 这个项目把有经验的机修工培养成工人教师。

e.en: A {worker-teacher} explained the machine in plain language.
e.zh: 一位工人教师用通俗的话讲解了这台机器。

e.en: Each {worker-technician} received safety training before entering the plant.
e.zh: 每名工人技师进厂前都接受了安全培训。

e.en: The repair was handled by a skilled {worker-technician}.
e.zh: 这次维修由一名熟练的技术工人处理。

workerist.t: 工人主义者；偏重工人阶级的

e.en: His politics remained strongly {workerist}.
e.zh: 他的政治立场仍带有强烈的工人主义色彩。

e.en: The essay criticized the party's {workerist} assumptions.
e.zh: 那篇文章批评了该党偏重工人阶级的预设。

e.en: An old {workfellow} visited him after retirement.
e.zh: 一位老同事在他退休后来看望了他。

e.en: She trusted her {workfellow} with the difficult repair.
e.zh: 她把这项困难的维修交给信得过的工友。

e.en: The inn was full of tired {workfolk} at dusk.
e.zh: 黄昏时，客栈里满是疲惫的劳动者。

e.en: Local {workfolk} shared stories after the harvest.
e.zh: 当地干活的人们在收获后分享故事。

e.en: The {workfolks} gathered outside the mill.
e.zh: 工友们聚集在磨坊外。

e.en: She cooked a large meal for the {workfolks}.
e.zh: 她给那些劳动者们做了一大顿饭。

e.en: The novel follows a young {workgirl} in the city.
e.zh: 这部小说讲述一个年轻女工在城里的生活。

e.en: A {workgirl} carried parcels through the market.
e.zh: 一个做工的女孩提着包裹穿过市场。

e.en: The farmer hired another {workhand} for the summer.
e.zh: 农场主又雇了一名夏季雇工。

e.en: Every {workhand} on the crew knew the routine.
e.zh: 队里的每个干活人手都熟悉这套流程。

e.en: Repeated bending caused {workhardening} in the metal strip.
e.zh: 反复弯折使金属条产生了加工硬化。

e.en: Engineers reduced {workhardening} by changing the forming process.
e.zh: 工程师通过改变成形工艺来减少冷作硬化。

e.en: The machinist tightened the {workholder} before cutting.
e.zh: 机加工工人在切削前拧紧了工件夹具。

e.en: A reliable {workholder} keeps the part steady.
e.zh: 可靠的工件夹具能让零件保持稳定。

workin.t: 静坐式抗议；工作场抗争

e.en: Employees staged a {workin} to protest the closure.
e.zh: 员工举行静坐式抗议，反对工厂关闭。

e.en: The union called the {workin} a peaceful action.
e.zh: 工会称这次工作场抗争是和平行动。

working-class.t: 工人阶级的；劳动阶层的

e.en: He grew up in a {working-class} neighborhood.
e.zh: 他在一个工人阶级社区长大。

e.en: The film shows {working-class} life without sentimentality.
e.zh: 这部电影不煽情地展现了劳动阶层的生活。

working-classization.t: 工人阶级化；劳动阶层化

e.en: The scholar described the town's {working-classization} after the factories opened.
e.zh: 那位学者描述了工厂开办后该镇的工人阶级化。

e.en: Rapid {working-classization} changed local politics.
e.zh: 迅速的劳动阶层化改变了当地政治。

e.en: A {working-group} will review the safety rules.
e.zh: 一个工作组将审查安全规则。

e.en: The treaty was drafted by a small {working-group}.
e.zh: 这份条约由一个小型专题小组起草。

e.en: The {working-out} of the plan took months.
e.zh: 这个计划的落实过程花了几个月。

e.en: Show your {working-out} below the answer.
e.zh: 请在答案下方写出你的计算过程。

e.en: She was the first {workingwoman} in her family.
e.zh: 她是家里第一位职业女性。

e.en: The portrait shows a tired {workingwoman} leaving the mill.
e.zh: 这幅画像描绘了一名疲惫的女工离开工厂。

e.en: The article discussed childcare for {workingwomen}.
e.zh: 那篇文章讨论了职业女性们的育儿问题。

e.en: Several {workingwomen} spoke at the union meeting.
e.zh: 几名女工在工会会议上发了言。

e.en: The town had many {workless} young people.
e.zh: 镇上有许多失业的年轻人。

e.en: He felt useless during those {workless} months.
e.zh: 在那几个月无工作的日子里，他觉得自己毫无用处。

e.en: Long {worklessness} can damage confidence.
e.zh: 长期失业状态会损害自信。

e.en: The report links {worklessness} with poor health.
e.zh: 报告把无工作与健康状况不佳联系起来。

e.en: The {workmaster} assigned each mason a task.
e.zh: 工头给每个石匠分派了任务。

e.en: A strict {workmaster} watched the apprentices closely.
e.zh: 一位严厉的作业主管密切看着学徒们。

e.en: The oil company scheduled a {workover} for the well.
e.zh: 石油公司安排对这口井进行修井。

e.en: The old engine needs a complete {workover}.
e.zh: 这台旧发动机需要彻底整修。

e.en: The supervisor handed each team a {workpack}.
e.zh: 主管给每个小组发了一份工作包。

e.en: A clear {workpack} reduces mistakes on site.
e.zh: 清晰的作业资料包能减少现场错误。

e.en: The survey team carried {workpacks} into the hills.
e.zh: 调查队把工作背包带进了山里。

e.en: Each technician received two new {workpacks} for field repairs.
e.zh: 每位技术员都领到了两个用于现场维修的新工作包。

e.en: The auditor filed each {workpaper} with the final report.
e.zh: 审计员把每份工作底稿同最终报告一起归档。

e.en: Her {workpaper} outlined a new approach to housing policy.
e.zh: 她的工作论文概述了一种新的住房政策思路。

e.en: The engineer adjusted the machine's {workpoint} to reduce vibration.
e.zh: 工程师调整了机器的工作点以减少振动。

e.en: At this {workpoint}, the circuit remains stable under load.
e.zh: 在这个操作点上，电路在负载下仍保持稳定。

e.en: Their {workship} improved after the roles became clearer.
e.zh: 职责更清楚后，他们的工作关系有所改善。

e.en: Good {workship} depends on trust as much as skill.
e.zh: 良好的协作状态既依赖信任，也依赖能力。

e.en: Place the bicycle on the {workstand} before removing the wheel.
e.zh: 拆车轮前，先把自行车放到维修支架上。

e.en: The old {workstand} held drills, clamps, and spare parts.
e.zh: 旧工作台上放着钻头、夹具和备件。

e.en: The doctor ordered a full {workup} after the fainting spell.
e.zh: 她晕倒后，医生安排了一整套检查评估。

e.en: The orchestra began its {workup} for the summer tour.
e.zh: 管弦乐团开始为夏季巡演逐步排练准备。

e.en: Factory employees must wear approved {workwear} on site.
e.zh: 工厂员工在现场必须穿规定的工作服。

e.en: The brand sells durable {workwear} for builders and mechanics.
e.zh: 这个品牌销售适合建筑工人和机械师的耐用工装。

e.en: {Workwise}, this month has been unusually quiet.
e.zh: 就工作而言，这个月异常清闲。

e.en: She is doing well {workwise}, but she wants more time at home.
e.zh: 从工作方面看她进展不错，但她想有更多时间在家。

e.en: The skilled {workwoman} repaired the carved wooden chair.
e.zh: 那位熟练的女工匠修好了雕花木椅。

e.en: A {workwoman} from the mill spoke at the meeting.
e.zh: 一名来自工厂的女工在会上发了言。

e.en: The {workwomen} organized for safer conditions in the factory.
e.zh: 女工们组织起来，要求工厂提供更安全的条件。

e.en: Several {workwomen} restored the old tapestries by hand.
e.zh: 几位女工匠手工修复了那些旧挂毯。

e.en: The new sprinter looks like a real {world-beater}.
e.zh: 这名新短跑运动员看起来像是真正的世界顶尖选手。

e.en: Their battery design could become a {world-beater}.
e.zh: 他们的电池设计可能成为世界领先的产品。

e.en: The company claims to have {world-beating} battery technology.
e.zh: 这家公司声称拥有世界领先的电池技术。

e.en: She delivered a {world-beating} performance in the final.
e.zh: 她在决赛中拿出了顶尖级的表现。

e.en: The city now has a {world-class} concert hall.
e.zh: 这座城市现在有了一座世界级音乐厅。

e.en: He trained with {world-class} coaches before the Olympics.
e.zh: 奥运会前，他跟随顶尖教练训练。

e.en: They visited the {world-famed} museum during their trip.
e.zh: 他们旅行期间参观了那座举世闻名的博物馆。

e.en: The chef returned to his {world-famed} restaurant in Paris.
e.zh: 那位主厨回到了他在巴黎那家举世闻名的餐厅。

e.en: They stayed near the {world-famous} beach.
e.zh: 他们住在那片世界闻名的海滩附近。

e.en: The singer became {world-famous} after one hit song.
e.zh: 这位歌手凭一首热门歌曲成了世界闻名的人物。

e.en: The poem speaks of a {world-old} sorrow.
e.zh: 这首诗写的是一种极古老的悲伤。

e.en: They followed a {world-old} custom at the harvest feast.
e.zh: 他们在丰收宴上遵循了一项世代相传的习俗。

e.en: A {world-renowned} surgeon led the operation.
e.zh: 一位举世闻名的外科医生主刀了这台手术。

e.en: The university is {world-renowned} for climate research.
e.zh: 这所大学因气候研究而举世闻名。

e.en: The discovery was hailed as a {world-shaking} breakthrough.
e.zh: 这一发现被誉为震撼世界的突破。

e.en: He promised {world-shaking} reforms but delivered little.
e.zh: 他承诺进行震撼世界的改革，但实际成果很少。

e.en: Travel changed her {world-view} in unexpected ways.
e.zh: 旅行以意想不到的方式改变了她的世界观。

e.en: His political {world-view} was shaped by childhood poverty.
e.zh: 他的政治世界观受到童年贫困经历的塑造。

e.en: A tone of {world-weariness} runs through the novel.
e.zh: 这部小说中贯穿着一种倦世的语气。

e.en: Her jokes hid a deep {world-weariness}.
e.zh: 她的玩笑掩盖着很深的厌世感。

e.en: The detective gave a {world-weary} sigh.
e.zh: 那名侦探发出一声厌世般的叹息。

e.en: She sounded {world-weary} after years in politics.
e.zh: 从政多年后，她听起来既倦怠又世故。

e.en: The young boxer was already being called a {worldbeater}.
e.zh: 这位年轻拳手已经被称作世界顶尖选手。

e.en: Their small engine proved to be a {worldbeater}.
e.zh: 他们的小型发动机证明是一款无敌产品。

e.en: The monk rejected a {worldful} life of comfort.
e.zh: 那位僧侣拒绝了充满尘世享乐的生活。

e.en: Her letters are {worldful}, crowded with markets and gossip.
e.zh: 她的信很世俗，满是市场见闻和闲谈。

e.en: The cafe became a quiet {worldlet} of artists and students.
e.zh: 那家咖啡馆成了艺术家和学生的小小天地。

e.en: Each story creates a separate {worldlet} with its own rules.
e.zh: 每个故事都创造出一个有自身规则的小世界。

e.en: The preacher warned the {worldling} against empty pleasures.
e.zh: 传教士告诫那个俗人不要沉迷空洞的享乐。

e.en: He played the charming {worldling} at court.
e.zh: 他在宫廷里扮演着迷人的世俗之人。

e.en: The abandoned chapel felt {worshipless} and cold.
e.zh: 那座废弃小礼拜堂显得无人礼拜，冷冷清清。

e.en: He imagined a {worshipless} age ruled only by profit.
e.zh: 他想象一个不再敬神、只受利润支配的时代。

e.en: The manuscript spells {worshipp} with an extra letter.
e.zh: 这份手稿把“worship”按旧式多写了一个字母。

e.en: They gathered to {worshipp} in the old chapel.
e.zh: 他们聚在那座老礼拜堂里敬拜。

e.en: The policy should help the {worst-off} families first.
e.zh: 这项政策应先帮助境况最差的家庭。

e.en: Even among the unemployed, he was one of the {worst-off}.
e.zh: 即使在失业者中，他也属于最穷困的一类。

e.en: She spent her savings on a {worthful} cause.
e.zh: 她把积蓄花在一项有价值的事业上。

e.en: His old letters seemed {worthful} after his death.
e.zh: 他去世后，那些旧信显得很有价值。

e.en: The hillside was dotted with {wortle} bushes.
e.zh: 山坡上点缀着一丛丛越橘灌木。

e.en: She made a dark jam from wild {wortles}.
e.zh: 她用野生越橘做了一罐深色果酱。

e.en: Thou {wost} the truth already.
e.zh: 你其实早已知道真相。

e.en: If thou {wost} his name, speak it now.
e.zh: 若你知道他的名字，现在就说出来。

e.en: He {wostteth} more than he admits.
e.zh: 他知道的比他承认的更多。

e.en: The scribe wrote that she {wostteth} the secret.
e.zh: 抄写员写道，她知道那个秘密。

e.en: {Wotcha}, mate, how have you been?
e.zh: 嘿，伙计，你最近怎么样？

e.en: She greeted him with a cheerful {wotcha}.
e.zh: 她快活地跟他说了声你好。

e.en: {Wotcher}, Harry, said the old woman.
e.zh: “你好啊，哈利，”老妇人说道。

e.en: He gave me a quick {wotcher} and hurried on.
e.zh: 他匆匆跟我打了声招呼就继续赶路。

e.en: He {wotchered} at everyone in the pub.
e.zh: 他在酒吧里见谁都用“你好啊”打招呼。

e.en: She {wotchered} cheerfully from the doorway.
e.zh: 她站在门口高兴地喊了声你好。

e.en: Thou {wotest} where the road ends.
e.zh: 你知道这条路通向哪里。

e.en: If thou {wotest} the answer, tell me.
e.zh: 如果你知道答案，就告诉我。

e.en: Thou {wottest} the danger well.
e.zh: 你很清楚其中的危险。

e.en: Since thou {wottest} his heart, judge kindly.
e.zh: 既然你了解他的心意，就宽厚地判断吧。

e.en: He {wotteth} nothing of our plan.
e.zh: 他对我们的计划一无所知。

e.en: The poet says love {wotteth} no law.
e.zh: 诗人说，爱情不懂法律的约束。

e.en: The {would-be} actor moved to London.
e.zh: 那个想当演员的人搬到了伦敦。

e.en: Police stopped the {would-be} thief at the door.
e.zh: 警察在门口拦住了那个企图行窃的人。

e.en: Thou {wouldest} help me if thou couldst.
e.zh: 若你能做到，你会帮助我的。

e.en: Why {wouldest} thou leave so soon?
e.zh: 你为何这么快就要离开？

e.en: Thou {wouldst} not betray a friend.
e.zh: 你不会背叛朋友。

e.en: If thou {wouldst} listen, I could explain.
e.zh: 如果你愿意听，我可以解释。

wound-up.t: 紧张烦躁的；上紧发条的

e.en: She was too {wound-up} to sleep.
e.zh: 她紧张得睡不着。

e.en: The {wound-up} toy marched across the table.
e.zh: 那只上紧发条的玩具在桌上走动。

e.en: Even the strongest hero remains {woundable}.
e.zh: 即使最强大的英雄也仍会受伤。

e.en: The exposed skin was {woundable} in battle.
e.zh: 裸露的皮肤在战斗中容易受伤。

e.en: He returned from the duel {woundless}.
e.zh: 他从决斗中归来，身上没有伤口。

e.en: The statue looked {woundless} despite the blast.
e.zh: 尽管经历爆炸，那座雕像看起来毫发无损。

e.en: The medic turned {woundward} to examine the cut.
e.zh: 医护人员转向伤口查看那道割伤。

e.en: He kept his shield {woundward} as he retreated.
e.zh: 他后退时把盾牌护在伤口那一侧。

e.en: The healer packed the cut with {woundwort}.
e.zh: 治疗者用伤草敷住那道伤口。

e.en: Purple {woundwort} grew beside the lane.
e.zh: 紫色的水苏属草本长在小路旁。

worldly-minded.t: 重视世俗利益的；现实的

e.en: His {worldly-minded} relatives urged him to choose a safer career.
e.zh: 他那些重视现实利益的亲戚劝他选择更稳妥的职业。

e.en: The monk warned against becoming too {worldly-minded}.
e.zh: 那位僧侣告诫人们不要过分贪恋世俗。

e.en: Her {worldly-mindedness} helped the charity negotiate better contracts.
e.zh: 她的现实头脑帮助慈善机构谈下了更好的合同。

e.en: The sermon criticized excessive {worldly-mindedness} among the faithful.
e.zh: 那篇布道批评信众中过度的世俗心态。

e.en: She gave him a {worldly-wise} smile after hearing the excuse.
e.zh: 听完那个借口后，她露出一个深谙世故的微笑。

e.en: A {worldly-wise} traveler avoids offers that seem too generous.
e.zh: 老练的旅行者会避开那些好得不真实的提议。

e.en: The old harbor grew into a busy {worldport}.
e.zh: 那座老港口发展成了繁忙的国际港口。

e.en: Singapore is often described as a modern {worldport}.
e.zh: 新加坡常被形容为一座现代世界性港城。

e.en: The preacher spoke as if {worldsday} were near.
e.zh: 那位传教士说得好像世界末日已经临近。

e.en: In the old poem, {worldsday} brings fire and judgment.
e.zh: 在那首古诗里，审判日带来了烈火与裁决。

worldward.t: 向着尘世的；面向世界地

e.en: After years alone, his thoughts turned {worldward} again.
e.zh: 多年独处之后，他的心思又转向了尘世。

e.en: The village opened its gates {worldward} after the war.
e.zh: 战后，这个村庄向外部世界敞开了大门。

e.en: The photographer chose a {worm's-eye} view of the tower.
e.zh: 摄影师选择从低处仰拍那座塔。

e.en: From a {worm's-eye} perspective, the desks looked enormous.
e.zh: 从贴近地面的视角看，那些书桌显得巨大。

e.en: They found a {worm-eaten} chest in the attic.
e.zh: 他们在阁楼里发现了一只被虫蛀的箱子。

e.en: The policy rested on {worm-eaten} ideas about class.
e.zh: 这项政策建立在腐朽的阶级观念之上。

e.en: The children tried {worm-fishing} beside the quiet pond.
e.zh: 孩子们在安静的池塘边试着用蚯蚓钓鱼。

e.en: He preferred {worm-fishing} to using artificial lures.
e.zh: 比起用假饵，他更喜欢用蚯蚓钓鱼。

e.en: A tiny {worm-hole} marked the antique table.
e.zh: 那张古董桌上有一个小小的虫蛀孔。

e.en: The novel sends explorers through a distant {worm-hole}.
e.zh: 那部小说让探险者穿过遥远的虫洞。

e.en: Fresh {wormcast} dotted the lawn after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后草坪上散布着新鲜的蚯蚓粪堆。

e.en: Gardeners value {wormcast} as a rich natural fertilizer.
e.zh: 园丁把蚓粪视为肥力很高的天然肥料。

e.en: This apple looks {wormier} than the others.
e.zh: 这个苹果看起来比其他几个虫蛀得更厉害。

e.en: His second excuse sounded even {wormier}.
e.zh: 他的第二个借口听起来更加可疑。

e.en: She threw away the {wormiest} peaches first.
e.zh: 她先把虫蛀最严重的桃子扔掉了。

e.en: That was the {wormiest} explanation he had offered all week.
e.zh: 那是他这一周给出的最可疑的解释。

e.en: The farmer was pleased with the {wormless} fruit.
e.zh: 农夫对这些没有虫的水果很满意。

e.en: The vet confirmed the puppy was {wormless} after treatment.
e.zh: 兽医确认小狗治疗后已无寄生虫。

e.en: A pale {wormling} curled under the stone.
e.zh: 一条苍白的小虫蜷在石头下面。

e.en: The fantasy story follows a brave little {wormling}.
e.zh: 那个奇幻故事讲述了一只勇敢小虫的经历。

e.en: The herbalist kept dried {wormseed} in a glass jar.
e.zh: 草药师把晒干的驱虫草籽放在玻璃罐里。

e.en: Old remedies used {wormseed} against intestinal parasites.
e.zh: 旧时疗法用土荆芥籽来对付肠道寄生虫。

e.en: The stairs were {worn-down} by decades of use.
e.zh: 这些楼梯因几十年的使用而磨损。

e.en: She felt {worn-down} after months of caring for him.
e.zh: 照顾他几个月后，她感到疲惫不堪。

e.en: I was {worn-out} after the long flight.
e.zh: 长途飞行后我筋疲力尽。

e.en: He replaced his {worn-out} shoes before the trip.
e.zh: 旅行前他换掉了那双穿坏的鞋。

e.en: For one {worriless} afternoon, they forgot the bills.
e.zh: 在那个无忧无虑的下午，他们忘记了账单的烦恼。

e.en: His {worriless} manner annoyed colleagues under pressure.
e.zh: 他那副无忧无虑的样子让压力中的同事很恼火。

e.en: Money was a constant {worriment} during those years.
e.zh: 那些年里，钱一直是个持续的烦恼。

e.en: She tried to hide her {worriment} from the children.
e.zh: 她努力不让孩子们看出自己的忧虑。

e.en: Do not {worrit} yourself over every small delay.
e.zh: 不要为每一次小小的延误烦扰自己。

e.en: The old aunt would {worrit} about the weather for days.
e.zh: 那位老姨妈会为天气担心好几天。

e.en: They grilled {wors} over the coals at sunset.
e.zh: 日落时他们在炭火上烤南非香肠。

e.en: The market sells spicy {wors} by the kilogram.
e.zh: 市场按公斤出售辛辣的南非香肠。

e.en: Families were {worse-off} after the factory closed.
e.zh: 工厂关闭后，许多家庭的境况更差了。

e.en: You may be {worse-off} if the fees increase.
e.zh: 如果费用上涨，你可能会更吃亏。

e.en: The doctor noted a sudden {worsement} in his condition.
e.zh: 医生注意到他的病情突然恶化。

e.en: They feared the {worsement} of relations between the two towns.
e.zh: 他们担心两个城镇之间的关系变坏。

woundy.t: 受伤的；多伤口的；伤感的

e.en: The old soldier showed his {woundy} arm to the doctor.
e.zh: 那位老兵把满是伤痕的手臂给医生看。

e.en: Her diary had a {woundy} tone after the quarrel.
e.zh: 争吵之后，她的日记里带着一种受伤的语气。

e.en: The hunter dipped the dart in {wourali} before entering the forest.
e.zh: 猎人进森林前把飞镖蘸上箭毒汁。

e.en: Early travelers wrote fearful reports about {wourali} and its effects.
e.zh: 早期旅行者曾写下关于箭毒及其作用的可怕记述。

wowser.t: 道德卫士；扫兴古板的人

e.en: Only a {wowser} would complain about dancing at a wedding.
e.zh: 只有那种古板扫兴的人才会抱怨婚礼上跳舞。

e.en: The columnist mocked the council as a pack of {wowsers}.
e.zh: 专栏作家嘲笑议会是一群道德卫士。

woylie.t: 刷尾负鼠；澳洲小有袋兽

e.en: A {woylie} searched for seeds under the dry leaves.
e.zh: 一只刷尾负鼠在干叶下面寻找种子。

e.en: Conservationists released several {woylies} into the protected woodland.
e.zh: 保护人员把几只刷尾负鼠放归受保护的林地。

e.en: The coast bore the marks of a {wrackful} storm.
e.zh: 海岸上留下了一场毁灭性风暴的痕迹。

e.en: He remembered those {wrackful} days after the trial.
e.zh: 他想起审判之后那些充满痛苦的日子。

e.en: Mist seemed to {wraithe} around the ruined tower.
e.zh: 雾气似乎像幽灵一样环绕着废塔。

e.en: Her pale face would {wraithe} in his memory at night.
e.zh: 夜里，她苍白的脸会幽灵般浮现在他的记忆中。

e.en: The old ballad says he took the {wrang} road home.
e.zh: 那首古老民谣说他走错了回家的路。

e.en: She felt the judgment was {wrang} from the start.
e.zh: 她觉得这个判决从一开始就是错的。

wranglership.t: 数学优等生称号；辩论者身份

e.en: His {wranglership} at Cambridge brought his family great pride.
e.zh: 他在剑桥获得数学优等生称号，让家人十分自豪。

e.en: The essay treats {wranglership} as a habit of constant argument.
e.zh: 这篇文章把善辩者身份视为一种不断争论的习惯。

e.en: The manager gave a quick {wrap-up} after the meeting.
e.zh: 会议结束后，经理做了一个简短总结。

e.en: We watched the news {wrap-up} before going to bed.
e.zh: 睡前我们看了新闻总结节目。

e.en: The parcel arrived with too much plastic {wrappage}.
e.zh: 包裹送到时用了太多塑料包装材料。

e.en: The shop charges extra for decorative {wrappage}.
e.zh: 这家店会对装饰性包装另行收费。
